children.text: bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdās tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyetaiṣa hy artho vidhīyate || Jaim_2,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Action-words (<s>karmaśabda</s>) denote existence (<s>bhāva</s>); from them, action (<s>kriyā</s>) is understood — for this is the meaning that is enjoined. || <s>Jaim</s>. 2.1.1 ||

children.text:
saṃbandhaṃ tāval lakṣaṇadvayasya karoti |
tatra prathame 'dhyāye pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ vṛttam ity uktam |
tad ayuktam |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: First, he establishes the connection of the two defining characteristics. Therein, it has been stated that in the first chapter the definition of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa</s>) was completed. That is not correct. Why?

children.text: naiva hi prathame 'dhyāye sūtrakāreṇa kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: For in the first chapter, by the <s>sūtra</s>-maker, nothing whatsoever

children.text: lakṣaṇena pramāṇādeḥ svarūpam upavarṇitam // 1 //
children.translated_text: of the true nature of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the like has been described by means of a definition. // 1 //

children.text:
tan nāma lakṣaṇam ucyate yena tadvyatiriktebhyas tasya svarūpaṃ vyāvṛttākāraṃ nirūpyate |
na caivaṃ pramāṇādilakṣaṇam uktam |
anumānādīni tāvan naiva sūtritāni |
pratyakṣam api dharmaṃ praty animittatvenopanyastaṃ na lakṣyatveneti vyākhyātam |
na ca śabdo 'pi dharmapramāṇabhūtaḥ kaścil lakṣitaḥ, asminn evādhikaraṇe tasya lakṣyamāṇatvāt |
yad api vṛttikāreṇa sarveṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pradarśitaṃ na tad adhyāyārthatvenopasaṃhartuṃ yuktam |
sūtrādhyāyārthānupasaṃhārāt |
kathaṃ ca samastalakṣaṇārthavyatirikta evārthe sūtrāṇi kṣīyeran |
api ca
children.translated_text: A definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is that by which the true nature of something, in its aspect as distinguished from other things, is ascertained. But the definition of the means of valid knowledge and the like has not been stated in this way. Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and the other [means of knowledge] were not formulated in <s>sūtras</s> at all. Even perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) was presented as a non-indicator (<s>animitta</s>) with respect to <s>dharma</s>, not as something to be defined — so it has been explained. Nor has any particular verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) that serves as a means of knowing <s>dharma</s> been defined, since it is being defined precisely in this very topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). Although the commentator (<s>vṛttikāra</s>) has shown the definition of all [means of knowledge], it is not proper to summarize that as the purport of the chapter, because the purport of the chapter must follow from the <s>sūtras</s> [alone]. And how could the <s>sūtras</s> be exhausted in a meaning that is entirely different from the purpose of a complete definition? Moreover,

children.text: vṛttikāreṇa yo 'py uktaḥ ṣaṭkaḥ pratyakṣapūrvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the six [means of valid knowledge] beginning with perception, which were stated by the commentator (<s>vṛttikāra</s>),

children.text: aparīkṣyatayā so 'pi naiva lakṣaṇagocaraḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: since they were stated as not requiring examination, they too do not fall within the scope of definition. // 2 //

children.text:
%p. 59
lokaprasiddhārthāni hi tāny aparīkṣyatvenoktāni na prathamādhyāyaviṣayatvenopasaṃhāram arhanti |
tasmād yat prathame 'dhyāye vṛttaṃ tad ālocyaitad bhāṣyaṃ neyam |
tatra
children.translated_text: [p. 59] For those [means of knowledge], being stated as well-known in common parlance and therefore as not requiring examination, do not deserve to be summarized as the subject matter of the first chapter. Therefore, having considered what was accomplished in the first chapter, this commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) should be understood accordingly. Therein:

children.text: pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ tāvac codanālakṣaṇāśrayam /
children.translated_text: The definition of the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa-lakṣaṇa</s>) rests upon the definition of injunction (<s>codanā-lakṣaṇa</s>);

children.text: vidhyāditattvanirṇītiḥ pramāṇenaiva ca sthitā // 3 //
children.translated_text: and the determination of the true nature of injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) and the like is established only through the means of valid knowledge. // 3 //

children.text:
samasto hi prathamaḥ pādaś codanālakṣaṇasūtraparikaraḥ |
tatra ca dharmasya codanālakṣaṇatvam uktam |
ato 'vadhāritārthalakṣaṇaśabdasāhacaryāt pramāṇaśabdaḥ pramīyate ity evaṃ vyutpādya dharmaviṣaya eva vyākhyeyaḥ |
saty api prameyamātravācitve 'smin śāstre jijñāsyatvena dharmaḥ prakrānta iti sa eva gṛhyate |
children.translated_text: For the entire first section (<s>pāda</s>) is an ancillary to the <s>sūtra</s> on the definition of injunction (<s>codanā-lakṣaṇa</s>). Therein, it was stated that <s>dharma</s> has injunction as its defining characteristic. Therefore, due to the association with the words 'defining characteristic' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and 'ascertained meaning' (<s>avadhāritārtha</s>), the word <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), having been etymologically derived as 'that by which one knows,' should be explained only with reference to <s>dharma</s>. Even though it may denote any object of knowledge in general, in this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) <s>dharma</s> has been introduced as the subject of inquiry, and therefore only <s>dharma</s> is taken [as the referent].

children.text:
atha vā karaṇam eva pramāṇam, tasyaiva lakṣaṇam uktam |
yady api ca sarvapramāṇānāṃ tan noktaṃ tathāpi dharmapramāṇasya codanātvaṃ nāma lakṣaṇam ity etāvataivoktaṃ manyate |
na cāvaśyaṃ sarvātmanaiva lakṣite lakṣaṇatvam |
viśeṣarūpāṇām ānantyena sarvalakṣaṇābhā-
%p. 60
vaprasaṅgāt |
api cautpattikasūtreṇa viśeṣo 'py ukta eva yenāgamaviśeṣo gamyate |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the means (<s>karaṇa</s>) itself is the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and its definition has been stated. Even though the definition of all means of valid knowledge has not been given, nevertheless, the definition of the means of knowing <s>dharma</s> — namely, that it is of the nature of injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — this much alone is considered to have been stated. And it is not necessary that a definition characterize [the definiendum] in its entirety, [p. 60] because due to the infinity of specific forms, the absurd consequence would arise that no definition of anything is possible. Moreover, by the <s>sūtra</s> on the innate [connection of word and meaning] (<s>autpattika-sūtra</s>), a specific distinction has indeed been stated by which the particular nature of scriptural tradition (<s>āgama</s>) is understood.

children.text:
atha vopanyastasya codanātmakasya pramāṇasya lakṣaṇaṃ prāmāṇyakāraṇam uktam ity upasaṃhāraḥ |
tathā yady api vidher idaṃ rūpam idam arthavādasyedaṃ mantrasyety evaṃ noktaṃ tathāpi dharmaṃ praty upayogābhidhānāt tattvaṃ nirṇītam |
avasarābhāvāt tu tatsvarūpaṃ na nirdiṣṭam |
śrutimūlatvaṃ vijñānasya smṛtiprāmāṇye tattvam |
nāmadheyasya codanāntargatatvāt pramāṇatvam |
saṃdigdhārthanirṇaye vākyaśeṣasāmarthyayoḥ prāmāṇyam ity evaṃ samastam adhyāyaṃ pramāṇalakṣaṇam ācakṣate |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, the summary is that the definition of the means of valid knowledge that has been presented — which is of the nature of injunction (<s>codanā</s>) — states the cause of its validity (<s>prāmāṇya-kāraṇa</s>). Likewise, even though it has not been stated that 'this is the form of an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), this is [the form] of an explanatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), this is [the form] of a <s>mantra</s>,' nevertheless, since their utility with respect to <s>dharma</s> has been declared, their true nature has been determined. However, their specific form has not been indicated due to the absence of an appropriate occasion. The fact that cognition has its root in scripture (<s>śruti</s>) constitutes the truth regarding the validity of tradition (<s>smṛti</s>). The means-of-knowledge status of a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>) [derives from] its being included within injunction. The validity of contextual completion (<s>vākyaśeṣa</s>) and indicative power (<s>sāmarthya</s>) lies in the determination of doubtful meaning — thus they call the entire chapter the definition of the means of valid knowledge.

children.text:
tan na prasmartavyam iti |
avismṛtaprāmāṇyo hi bhedādipratipādanam aviśeṣād anarthakaṃ hi syāt iti kriyamāṇaṃ sahate |
anyathā hy anarthakaṃ nāmety api pratyavatiṣṭheta |
children.translated_text: That should not be forgotten. For one who has not forgotten the [established] means of valid knowledge, the teaching of distinctions and the like would be purposeless owing to non-differentiation — thus, when it is done [i.e., the teaching of distinctions is undertaken], it is justified. Otherwise, one might object that it is indeed purposeless.

children.text:
nanu pradhānāpradhānacintā tṛtīyacaturthayor viṣayaḥ katham atropanyasyate |
kecid āhuḥ |
iha dravyakarmaṇor uttaratra tu karmaṇām eva guṇapradhānatvavicārād apaunaruktyam iti |
tad ayuktam |
dravyaguṇasaṃskāreṣu ity atra sarvābhidhānāt |
tenaivaṃ vācyam
children.translated_text: Objection: The investigation of principal and subordinate is the subject matter of the third and fourth [chapters]; how then is it introduced here? Some say: Because here the principal-subordinate investigation concerns substances (<s>dravya</s>) and actions (<s>karman</s>), while later it concerns actions alone — hence there is no repetition. That is incorrect, because in [the sūtra] 'with respect to substances, qualities, and preparatory rites' (<s>dravya-guṇa-saṃskāreṣu</s>), all [three] are mentioned. Therefore, it should be stated thus:

children.text: lakṣaṇārtho 'tra tattvena bhedaḥ śabdāntarādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning of the [second chapter's] definition is truly distinction (<s>bheda</s>), [established] through different names and the like;

children.text: tam anv apūrvabhedo 'pi prādhānyaṃ tatprasiddhaye // 4 //
children.translated_text: Following that, the distinction of <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen transcendent result) too, and the [investigation of] principalness, [is undertaken] for the establishment thereof. // 4 //

children.text:
karmabhedas tāvad autsargiko lakṣaṇārthaḥ, tadapavādatvenābhedaḥ |
tadanuniṣpādinau tv apūrvabhedābhedau |
tatra pratikarmabhedam apūrvabhedaprasaktau tṛtīyasiddhaḥ pradhānāpradhānavicāraḥ punar apavādatvenārapsyate |
saty apy avahantyādīnāṃ śabdāntarādibhir bhede karmākāṅkṣitadṛṣṭaprayojanaparyavasānān na kriyājanyāpūrvāntarotpattiḥ |
yat tu niyamāpūrvaṃ tat kriyākṛtaṃ na bhavatīti na tayā vyapadiśyate |
tena yatraiva dravyādīni prati kriyāṇāṃ pradhānatvaṃ tatraiva tadbhedanimittāpūrvabhedasiddhiḥ |
asya ca vivekārthaṃ yad guṇapradhānalakṣaṇaṃ vakṣyate tadapavādāpavādārthaṃ dharmamātre tu stutaśastrayoḥ iti cādhikaraṇadvayaṃ prastoṣyate |
tataś cākhyātadvaividhye 'vadhārite prasaṅgāt tṛtīyaṃ prakāram abhidhāyakatvaṃ pratipādayituṃ mantraprastāvaḥ |
tallakṣaṇādīni tu prasaktānuprasaktena yāvat pādasamāpti |
tataḥ śabdāntarābhyāsābhyāṃ bhedam uktvā paurṇamāsyadhikaraṇenābhyāsāpavādaḥ kariṣyate samudāyānuvādatvāt |
tatas tadapavādārtham upāṃśuyājāghārāgnihotrapaśusomādhikaraṇāni |
tataḥ saṃkhyāsaṃjñāguṇair bhedaḥ |
tāvac ca guṇagato vicāro yāvat prakaraṇāntarādhikaraṇam |
tatas tannyāyānuvṛttir ā śākhāntarādhikaraṇāt |
tatra ca ṣaṭkātiriktabhedakāraṇavyudāsaḥ saṃjñābhyāsaguṇaprakriyāṇāṃ cāśaṅkānivṛttir ity etāvān bhedalakṣaṇārthaḥ |
eṣa evārtho 'vaśyaṃ vaktavyo 'ṅgāṅgitvādyavadhāraṇārtham |
na
%p. 62
cānyasyedānīm avasaro 'stīty ayam evādhyāyasaṃbandhaḥ |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The distinction of ritual actions (<s>karma-bheda</s>) is, as a general rule, the purpose of the definition [chapter]; the non-distinction [i.e., unity of actions] is an exception to that. The distinction and non-distinction of <s>apūrva</s> are dependent on and produced after that [distinction of actions]. Therein, when the distinction of <s>apūrva</s> follows from the distinction of each individual action, the investigation of principal and subordinate — established in the third [chapter] — will again be undertaken as an exception. Even though there is distinction of [actions like] <s>avahanty</s> and the like through different names and other [factors], since the action terminates in the seen purpose desired by the ritual — there is no production of a separate <s>apūrva</s> from the action. But the <s>apūrva</s> that is [established] by restriction (<s>niyama</s>) is not produced by the action, and therefore is not designated by it. Hence, only where there is principalness of actions with respect to substances and the like — only there is the distinction of <s>apūrva</s> established by reason of [action-]distinction. For the purpose of discerning this, the definition of principal and subordinate (<s>guṇa-pradhāna-lakṣaṇa</s>) will be stated; and as an exception to that exception, two topics (<s>adhikaraṇas</s>) — 'but in <s>dharma</s> in general, [the role] of praise and censure' — will be introduced. Then, having ascertained the twofold nature of the verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>), the introduction of <s>mantras</s> will serve to establish, by way of connection, a third mode — namely, the capacity to denote. The definition of <s>mantras</s> and the like continues through connected and sub-connected topics until the end of the section. Thereafter, having stated distinction through different names and repetition, the <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> topic will serve as an exception to [distinction by] repetition, since it is a restatement of the aggregate. Then, as exceptions to that, [come] the topics of <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s>, <s>Āghāra</s>, <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Paśu</s>, and <s>Soma</s>. Then distinction through number, name, and quality. The investigation regarding quality continues up to the topic of another context (<s>prakaraṇāntara</s>). Then the continuation of that principle [extends] up to the topic of another Vedic branch (<s>śākhāntara</s>). Therein, the exclusion of causes of distinction beyond the six [mentioned ones], and the removal of doubts regarding the procedures of name, repetition, and quality — this much is the purpose of the definition of distinction. [p. 62] This very meaning must necessarily be stated for the purpose of determining the relationship of principal and subordinate parts (<s>aṅga-aṅgin</s>). And since there is no occasion for anything else at this point, this alone is the connection of [this] chapter. Why?

children.text: śeṣaśeṣyādayaḥ sarve karmabhedanibandhanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Subsidiary-principal relationships (<s>śeṣa-śeṣin</s>) and all the rest are dependent upon the distinction of ritual actions;

children.text: kārye jñāte 'dhikāraḥ syād upadeśe 'tideśadhīḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: When the [nature of the] effect is known, eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) [can be determined]; and in the case of direct instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>), [there arises] the understanding of extended application (<s>atideśa</s>). // 5 //

children.text:
prāk tāvat pramāṇalakṣaṇād vedārthavicārātmakatvān na kasyacid bhedalakṣaṇādeḥ prastāva ity uttarakālam ārambhaḥ |
tatrāpi śeṣaśeṣitvaṃ prayojakāprayojakatvaṃ kramaś ca bhinnānāṃ bhavatīti na bhedalakṣaṇāt prāg ārabhyate |
tathādhikāraḥ karmasvarūpe 'vadhārite tadyogyatayā śakyo nirūpayitum iti pañcāpi lakṣaṇāni pratīkṣate |
tathottaraḥ ṣaṭko 'tideśaviṣayatvād upadeśajñānādhīnasiddhiḥ samastaḥ samastaṃ pūrvaṣaṭkam apekṣate |
tataś ca pariśeṣasiddho 'yaṃ bhedalakṣaṇasya saṃbandha ity atrārabhyate |
children.translated_text: Prior to the definition of the means of valid knowledge, since [the inquiry] consists in the investigation of the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, there is no occasion for introducing the definition of distinction and the like — hence the commencement [of this chapter] is later. Even within this [later portion], since the subsidiary-principal relationship, the relationship of motivating and non-motivating [factors], and sequence pertain to [things that are] distinct, [their investigation] cannot begin before the definition of distinction. Likewise, eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) can be determined through fitness [of a person] only when the true nature of the ritual action has been ascertained — hence it awaits all five definitions. Similarly, the latter group of six [chapters], since its subject matter is extended application (<s>atideśa</s>), depends for its establishment on the knowledge of direct instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>) — the entire [latter group] presupposes the entire former group of six. Therefore, the connection of the definition of distinction is established by the method of residual elimination, and hence [the discussion] begins here.

children.text:
ṣaḍvidhaḥ karmabhedaḥ iti sādhanabhedopacārāt |
vakṣyamāṇasūtrakramānurodhena nāmadheyaṃ saṃkhyānantaraṃ paṭhitavyaṃ sad anādarād ante paṭhitam |
itikaraṇo hetvarthaḥ |
ṣaḍvidhaḥ karmabheda etaiḥ kāraṇair iti yāvat |
atha vā karaṇe bhedaśabdaṃ vyutpādya sāmānādhikaraṇyenaiva śabdāntarādīni vyākhyeyāni |
saṃjñāśabdāntarayoḥ saṃkhyāguṇayoś cāpaunaruktyaṃ svasthāne vakṣyāmaḥ |
sarvadā caiṣāṃ bhinnaviṣayatvān na śrutyādivad
%p. 63
balābalacintā bhaviṣyatīti tadbhedapratipādanamātraṃ tātparyeṇa |
anyad upodghātādinā |
tatra
children.translated_text: The distinction of ritual actions is sixfold — this is stated by way of figuratively [attributing distinction to the actions from] the distinction of the means [of distinguishing]. According to the order of the <s>sūtras</s> to be discussed, the name (<s>nāmadheya</s>) should have been read immediately after number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), but due to its [relative] unimportance, it has been read at the end. The word <s>iti</s> has the sense of reason (<s>hetu</s>) — [i.e.,] the distinction of ritual actions is sixfold, [arising] from these causes. Alternatively, having etymologically derived the word <s>bheda</s> (distinction) in the instrumental sense [i.e., 'by means of'], [p. 63] the terms 'different name' (<s>śabdāntara</s>) and the like should be explained through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). The non-redundancy of name and different name, and of number and quality, we shall discuss in their proper places. And since these always have different domains, there will be no investigation of relative strength as in the case of [conflicting] <s>śruti</s> (scriptural text) and the like — hence the mere establishment of their [respective] distinctions is the primary purport. Everything else is by way of introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>) and the like. Therein:

children.text: cintāṃ prakṛtasiddhyarthām upodghātaṃ pracakṣate /
children.translated_text: They call an 'introduction' (<s>upodghāta</s>) a discussion undertaken for the purpose of establishing the matter at hand;

children.text: prasaktānuprasaktādi prastutād upajāyate // 6 //
children.translated_text: Connected and sub-connected [topics] arise from the topic under discussion. // 6 //

children.text: yathedam evādhikaraṇaṃ prakṛtānuniṣpādyapūrvabhedānusārasiddhyartham upodghātatvena bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: Just as this very topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) will serve as an introduction for the purpose of establishing the distinction of <s>apūrva</s>, which is to be subsequently determined in connection with the matter at hand.

children.text:
%p. 64
katarasmāt padāt phalena saṃbadhyamānād apūrvabhedābhedāv anugantavyāv iti |
yadā niravayavau vākyavākyārthau syātāṃ tataḥ kiṃ pratipadaṃ dharma ityādir asaṃbaddha eva vicāraḥ syāt, ata āha vākye ca padānām arthāḥ iti |
atrāpi codyate |
children.translated_text: [p. 64] From which word, when connected with its result, should the distinction and non-distinction of <s>apūrva</s> be traced? If sentence and sentence-meaning were without parts, then what? — the investigation 'Is <s>dharma</s> [to be determined] word by word?' would be entirely disconnected. Therefore he says: 'And the meanings of the words in a sentence' (<s>vākye ca padānām arthāḥ</s>). Here too an objection is raised:

children.text: codanālakṣaṇatvena vākyārtho 'vasthito yadā /
children.translated_text: When the sentence-meaning is established as having the character of injunction (<s>codanā-lakṣaṇa</s>),

children.text: dharmaḥ pratipadaṃ vācyaḥ katham āśaṅkyate tadā // 7 //
children.translated_text: how can it be suspected that <s>dharma</s> is to be stated word by word? // 7 //

children.text:
yadi hi dharmasvarūpam abhidhīyeta tataḥ kiṃ padena padenocyate iti vicāro yujyate, lākṣaṇike tv ayuktaḥ |
tad ucyate |
children.translated_text: If indeed the essential nature of <s>dharma</s> were being expressed, then the inquiry 'by which word is it designated?' would be appropriate. But in the case of a figurative [definition], it is inappropriate. To this it is said:

children.text: dharmatvaṃ phalasaṃbandhāt padārthasyaiva yujyate /
children.translated_text: The property of being <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmatva</s>) is justified only for the meaning of a word (<s>padārtha</s>), by virtue of [its] connection with the result (<s>phala</s>).

children.text: tat kim ekasya sarveṣām iti yuktā vicāraṇā // 8 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the inquiry 'whether of one [word] or of all [words]?' is appropriate. // 8 //

children.text:
na cātra yo dharmaḥ sa kiṃ padena padenocyata ity evaṃ vicāryate, kiṃ tarhi, yaḥ padena padenocyate sa kiṃ phalasaṃbandhottarakālaṃ vākyārthātmanā gamyamāno dharmo bhavati, athetarapadārthānugṛhīta ekaḥ padārtha iti |
tathā ca sarvair ekasya dharmatvaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavati |
sākṣāt phalasādhanamātrasya dharmatvābhyupagamāt |
na tu sarveṣām ekaḥ kaścid artho 'sti yaḥ sarvair ekaḥ ity evam āśrīyeta |
yac ca phalapadena saha padaṃ saṃbadhyate tasyārthaṃ dharmam apūrvasādhanaṃ ca manyante |
tena kiṃ sarvāṇi padāni phalena saṃbadhyante kiṃ vaikam iti vicāraḥ |
kiṃ prāptaṃ |
pratipadam iti |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And here the inquiry is not 'that which is <s>dharma</s>, by which word is it designated?' Rather, [the question is:] 'that which is designated by a particular word — does it become <s>dharma</s> when understood as the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārtha</s>) after the connection with the result, or is it a single word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>) assisted by the other word-meanings?' And thus the <s>dharma</s>-hood of one [thing] would be established by all [the words], since <s>dharma</s>-hood is accepted as belonging only to that which directly accomplishes the result. But there is no single meaning of all [the words] that could be relied upon as 'one thing [expressed] by all [words].' And whatever word is connected with the result-word, they consider its meaning to be <s>dharma</s> and the means to <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency). Therefore the inquiry is: do all words connect with the result, or only one? What is the prima facie view (<s>prāpta</s>)? Each word [individually]. Why?

children.text: aikarūpyeṇa saṃbandhaḥ pradhānena ca sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Connection is established through uniformity (<s>aikarūpya</s>) and through the principal factor (<s>pradhāna</s>).

children.text: tasmāt phalapadenaiva sarvaṃ saṃbadhyate padam // 9 //
children.translated_text: Therefore every word connects with the result-word (<s>phala-pada</s>) alone. // 9 //

children.text:
%p. 65
yadi hi viśeṣo gamyete---idaṃ phalasaṃbandhayogyam, idaṃ na---iti, tataḥ kiṃcid eva saṃbadhyeta |
anavagamyamāne tu sarvāṇi padāni phalenaiva saṃbadhyante |
yadi caikaṃ phalasaṃbandhi, itarāṇi tatsaṃbandhīnīti kalpyate, tato vājapeyādhikaraṇanyāyenaikasya phalaṃ praty upādānavidhānaguṇabhāvāt, itarat tu praty uddeśānuvādaprādhānyād vairūpyanimittavākyabhedaprasaṅgaḥ |
sarveṣāṃ phalaṃ praty upādīyamānānām aikarūpyāt tantrasaṃbandhopapattiḥ |
children.translated_text: If a distinction were understood — 'this is suitable for connection with the result, this is not' — then only some [words] would connect. But when no [such distinction] is understood, all words connect with the result alone. And if one [word-meaning] is connected with the result while the others are postulated as connected with that [result-connected word-meaning], then by the principle of the <s>Vājapeya</s> topic (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), one [word-meaning] would have subsidiary status (<s>guṇabhāva</s>) through being taken up as a means for the result, while the other, due to the priority of statement and restatement (<s>uddeśānuvāda</s>), would entail the splitting of the sentence on account of formal dissimilarity (<s>vairūpya</s>). When all [word-meanings] are taken up with reference to the result, the fitness for a single integrated (<s>tantra</s>) connection is established due to their uniformity (<s>aikarūpya</s>).

children.text:
sarvaś ca sati saṃbhave guṇam atilaṅghya pradhānenaiva nityaṃ saṃbadhyate |
tasmāt sarveṣāṃ phalasaṃbandhād dharmatvaṃ |
tatra tu kiṃ satrivat pratyekaṃ kṛtsnaṃ phalaṃ sādhayanti, atha darśapūrṇamāsavat saṃhatya, tathā kiṃ vikalpena samuccayena vetyādi yatheṣṭaṃ kalpanīyam |
children.translated_text: And everything, when connection is possible, always connects with the principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) alone, passing over the subsidiary (<s>guṇa</s>). Therefore <s>dharma</s>-hood [belongs to] all [word-meanings] through [their] connection with the result. But whether they accomplish the entire result individually like the <s>sattra</s> [sacrifice], or collectively like the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> [sacrifice]; and further, whether by option (<s>vikalpa</s>) or by accumulation (<s>samuccaya</s>), etc. — that is to be determined as desired.

children.text:
tatra phalabhūmagarīyastvāt, ekaśabdopādānābhāvāt, satrivat pratyekaṃ sādhanaśaktyavagamāt sarvebhyaḥ pṛthak phalam iti pakṣaḥ |
atha vāruṇādinyāyenaikavākyopā-
%p. 66
dānāt saṃhatānāṃ phalam |
atha vaikena nirākāṅkṣatvān na tadānīm evetarasaṃbandhopapattiḥ, tasmād vikalpa iti |
atrābhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: In that case, because of the greater weight of the result-ground, because of the absence of the word 'one' (<s>eka</s>), and because of understanding the productive capacity of each individually like the <s>sattra</s>, the view is that there is a separate result from each. Alternatively, by the rule of the <s>Vāruṇādi</s> [sacrifice], from being taken up in a single sentence (<s>ekavākya</s>), the result is [produced] by [them all] combined. Or, because a single [word-meaning] is self-sufficient without expectation, and because the connection of the other [words] is not justified at that very [moment], therefore there is an option. To this it is said:

children.text: phalena yasya saṃbandhas tato 'pūrvaṃ prakalpyate /
children.translated_text: From that [word-meaning] which has connection with the result, <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency) is postulated.

children.text: tadalpatvopapattau ca na yuktā bahukalpanā // 10 //
children.translated_text: And when its being [produced by] few is established, the postulation of many is not justified. // 10 //

children.text:
yadi hi phalasaṃbandhamātraparyavasāyy eva vākyaṃ bhavet, tataḥ kadācid sarvāṇy api phalena saṃbadhyeran |
iha tu tāvanmātreṇāsiddher apūrvam anyat kalpayitavyam, tac cānupapattipramāṇakam |
tatraikāpūrvakalpanayopapanne vākye nādṛṣṭāntarakalpanāpramāṇam asti |
yo hy anekāny apūrvāṇi kalpayati, kalpayaty asāv ekam |
tac cet kalpitam, arthavattvād vākyasya kṣīṇānyathānupapattir nāpūrvāntarasya pramāṇaṃ bhavati |
tasmād ekam eva phalasaṃbandhi, tasmāc cāpūrvam, itarat phalavadupakārīty adhyavasīyate |
children.translated_text: If the sentence had its scope limited merely to connection with the result, then all [words] might connect with the result at some point. But here, since the matter is not accomplished by that much alone, <s>apūrva</s> must be postulated as something else; and that [postulation] has as its warrant [only] the impossibility of [accounting for the result] otherwise (<s>anupapatti</s>). When the sentence is accounted for by postulating a single <s>apūrva</s>, there is no warrant for postulating another unseen [potency]. For whoever postulates many <s>apūrvas</s> does [in effect] postulate one; and if that one is postulated, then because the sentence becomes meaningful, the impossibility-otherwise [argument] is exhausted, and there is no warrant for a further <s>apūrva</s>. Therefore, only one [word-meaning] is connected with the result; from that, [arises] <s>apūrva</s>; and the other [word-meanings] are determined as auxiliaries to the result-connected [one].

children.text:
na cātra virodho bhaviṣyati |
nāmadheyatvena parihārāt |
agatyā vā daśāpavitreṇa grahaṃ saṃmārṣṭi itivan matvarthalakṣaṇāśrayaṇāt |
arthākṣiptasādhyāṃśadvāreṇa vā dhātvarthair ātmīyakaraṇagrahaṇasiddheḥ |
children.translated_text: And there will be no contradiction here, because of resolution through the status of name-designation (<s>nāmadheyatva</s>); or, out of necessity, because of resorting to the definition of the <s>matvartha</s> [suffix] — as in 'he sweeps the fireplace with the ten impurities'; or because of the establishment through verbal root-meanings of the inclusion of one's own instrument, by way of the portion to be accomplished that is implied by the meaning.

children.text:
evaṃ sthite katarad ekaṃ saṃbadhyatām iti sarvathānekādṛṣṭakalpanāparihārād aniyamaprāptāu, ucyate |
%p. 67
children.translated_text: In this situation, [the question arises:] 'which single [word] connects [with the result]?' Since there is no avoiding the postulation of multiple unseen [potencies] in any case, when the impossibility of a fixed determination is reached, it is said:

children.text: pradhānaṃ phalasaṃbandhi tatsaṃbandhy aṅgam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: The principal (<s>pradhāna</s>) is connected with the result; that which is connected with it is considered a subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>).

children.text: pradhānāṅgatvam ekasya na caikatrāvakalpate // 11 //
children.translated_text: And the same one [thing] cannot be both principal and subsidiary in a single [sentence]. // 11 //

children.text:
na hy ekasmin vākye tad eva kadācit phalasaṃbandhāt pradhānam, kadācit phalavadupakārād aṅgaṃ yujyate |
niyatarūpatvād aṅgāṅgibhāvasya |
tasmān niyogenaivākhyātapadān nāmapadād vāpūrvapratītiḥ |
children.translated_text: For it is not possible that in one sentence the same thing is sometimes the principal because of its connection with the result, and sometimes a subsidiary because of assisting the result-connected [thing]. Because the relationship of principal and subsidiary (<s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>) has a fixed form. Therefore, the cognition of <s>apūrva</s> necessarily [arises] from the verbal ending (<s>ākhyāta-pada</s>) or from the nominal word (<s>nāma-pada</s>).

children.text:
%p. 68
kaḥ punar bhāvaḥ, ke vā bhāvaśabdāḥ iti---yāvantaḥ phalasaṃbaddheṣu vākyeṣv ākhyātaśabdāḥ yajati dadāti juhoti ity evamādayaḥ, teṣu pratyayārthaprādhānyāt, kartari ca lakārotpatteḥ, yāgādiviśiṣṭakartrabhidhānam, kathaṃcid vā viparyayāt kartṛviśiṣṭayāgādyabhidhānaṃ manvānasya praśnaḥ |
children.translated_text: What then is <s>bhāva</s> (effectuation)? And what are the <s>bhāva</s>-words? — All the verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta-śabda</s>) in sentences connected with results, such as yajati ('sacrifices'), dadāti ('gives'), juhoti ('offers'), etc. Among these, because the suffix-meaning is predominant, and because the verbal ending arises with reference to the agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), [the expression] denotes the agent qualified by the sacrifice etc.; or, by some reversal, one who considers it to denote the sacrifice etc. qualified by the agent — [that is] the question.

children.text: satyām api caikaparyanuyogenobhayaparyanuyogasiddhau---yo 'yaṃ yajanam ijyā yāgaḥ ity anudāhṛtyaiva bhāvārthatāṃ bravīti, tan nūnaṃ ke'py alaukikā bhāvaśabdā api---ity ubhayapraśnaḥ |
children.translated_text: And even though the question about both [interpretations] is established through the inquiry about one — he who states the <s>bhāva</s>-meaning without even citing <s>yajanam</s>, <s>ijyā</s>, <s>yāga</s> [as examples], surely [intends] the question about both: 'are there perhaps some non-ordinary <s>bhāva</s>-words too?'

children.text: siddhāntavādī tu---bhavater ṇijantāt er ac ity acpratyaye kṛte bhāvanāvicinaṃ bhāvaśabdaṃ vyutpādya, ākhyātasya cānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tatparatvaṃ kartrabhidhānapratiṣedhaṃ cābhipretyodāharati yajati dadāti iti |
children.translated_text: The proponent of the established view (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), however, derives the <s>bhāva</s>-word as expressing the meaning of <s>bhāvanā</s> (effectuation) by applying the suffix <s>ac</s> through the rule '<s>er ac</s>' to the <s>ṇij</s>-derivative of the root <s>bhū</s>; and, intending to establish the priority [of <s>ākhyāta</s>-words] for that meaning and to negate the designation of the agent, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), gives the examples yajati, dadāti.

children.text:
paraḥ punaḥ---bhavater ṇijantād anyena naiṣo 'rtho 'bhidhīyate, na cākhyātapratyayasyātra vyāpāraḥ, dhātvantarārthatvāt |
kāmaṃ tulyajātīyatvena dhātava eva brūyuḥ, te 'pi tu yāgādivacanatvād asamarthāḥ---iti matvāha nanu yāgadānahomaśabdāḥ iti |
atrocyate |
children.translated_text: The opponent, however, [argues]: 'This meaning is not expressed by anything other than the <s>ṇij</s>-derivative of <s>bhū</s>, and the <s>ākhyāta</s> suffix has no function here, since it [merely] expresses the meaning of another verbal root. Of course, because they are of the same class, verbal roots alone might express [this meaning], but they too, being words for <s>yāga</s> etc., are incapable.' Thinking thus, he says: 'But surely the words <s>yāga</s>, <s>dāna</s>, <s>homa</s> [also express bhāvanā].' To this it is said:

children.text: yāgadānādanusyūto bhāvanātmāvagamyate /
children.translated_text: The meaning of <s>bhāvanā</s> (effectuation), interwoven with [the meanings of] sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>), giving (<s>dāna</s>), etc., is understood

children.text: nityam ākhyātaśabdebhyas tasmād bhāvārthateṣyate // 12 //
children.translated_text: always from verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta-śabda</s>); therefore the view that [they have] the meaning of <s>bhāva</s> is accepted. // 12 //

children.text:
yāvān eva hy ananyalabhyo 'rthaḥ śabdād gamyate, sa sarvaḥ śabdārthaḥ |
sarvatra cākhyāte dhātvarthaś ca tadanuraktā ca bhāvanā vijñāyate |
tasmād bhāvārthatvavyapadeśaḥ |
tadvyatiriktās tu dravyaguṇaśabdā vijñāyanta eveti na pṛṣṭāḥ |
children.translated_text: For whatever meaning that cannot be obtained from any other [source] is understood from a [particular] word — all that is the meaning of that word. And in every verbal form, both the root-meaning (<s>dhātvārtha</s>) and <s>bhāvanā</s> conjoined with it are understood. Therefore the designation 'having the meaning of <s>bhāva</s>.' But substance-words (<s>dravya-śabda</s>) and quality-words (<s>guṇa-śabda</s>) are [also] understood [from the sentence], so they are not being asked about.

children.text: tatra dravyādiśabdānāṃ niṣpannārthābhidhāyinām /
children.translated_text: Of those substance-words etc. which designate already-accomplished entities (<s>niṣpannārtha</s>),

children.text: karaṇārthatvayogyatvāt prāpnoti phalasaṃgatiḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: because of their fitness for the status of instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>), they attain connection with the result (<s>phala</s>). // 13 //

children.text:
sarvatra hi phalaṃ sādhyatvāt siddharūpaṃ sādhanam apekṣate, na sādhyāntaram |
nāmārthaś ca siddhatvāt tadapekṣāpūraṇasamarthaḥ, nākhyātārthaḥ |
svayam eva sādhyatvāt |
children.translated_text: because it itself is something to be accomplished.

children.text: tasmāt dravyādibhiḥ phalam---iti prāpte, sūtreṇottaraṃ dīyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, when the prima facie conclusion is reached that 'the result [comes] from substance-words etc.,' the answer is given by the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdā ye tebhyo 'pūrvakriyāgatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those action-words (<s>karma-śabda</s>) which have the meaning of <s>bhāva</s> — from them the notion of <s>apūrva</s>-action arises.

children.text: taiḥ kuryād yajinā svargam eṣa hy artho vidhīyate // 14 //
children.translated_text: Through them, the sacrificer (<s>yajin</s>) should [produce] heaven (<s>svarga</s>) — this indeed is the meaning that is enjoined (<s>vidhīyate</s>). // 14 //

For everywhere, the result, being something to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), requires a means (<s>sādhana</s>) that is already established in nature, not another thing to be accomplished. And the nominal meaning (<s>nāmārtha</s>), being [already] established, is capable of fulfilling that requirement; not the verbal meaning (<s>ākhyātārtha</s>),

children.text:
phalasaṃbandho hetur apūrvapratipatteḥ |
saṃbandhaś cākāṅkṣāpūrvakaḥ |
sā ca bhāvaśabdebhyaḥ prasarpantī dṛśyate, na dravyaguṇaśabdebhyaḥ |
tasmād ākhyātebhyaḥ apūrvabhāvanā gamyate |
tatra ca dhātvarthasya karaṇatvapratipattiḥ, pratyāsatteḥ |
atas tenaiva phalakaraṇabhūtenānyathānupapattyāpūrvaṃ bhāvyata ity avadhāryate |
children.translated_text: Connection with the result is the basis for the cognition of <s>apūrva</s>. And connection presupposes expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>). That [expectancy] is seen to extend from <s>bhāva</s>-words (verbal forms), not from substance-words and quality-words. Therefore, from verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>), the <s>bhāvanā</s> (effectuation) that produces <s>apūrva</s> is understood. And therein, the root-meaning (<s>dhātvārtha</s>) is understood as having the status of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), due to proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>). Hence it is determined that <s>apūrva</s> is effected by that very [root-meaning] which serves as the instrument for the result, through the reasoning of otherwise-impossibility (<s>anyathānupapatti</s>).

children.text:
%p. 70
kathaṃ punar yajyādīn pṛthak kṛtya kevalapratyayavācya eva bhāvanārtho labhyate bhāvayet iti. kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: But how is the <s>bhāvanā</s>-meaning obtained as expressed by the suffix alone, having separated out the [root-meanings of] yaj etc.? — that is, as 'he should effect' (<s>bhāvayet</s>). From where?

children.text: abhidadhyuḥ svaśaktyā hi vidhimātraṃ liṅādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The [suffixes] <s>liṅ</s> etc. would express the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) alone by their own capacity.

children.text: ṇyantasya bhavater arthaḥ kenāṃśenābhidhīyate // 15 //
children.translated_text: By which portion is the meaning of the <s>ṇij</s>-derivative of <s>bhū</s> expressed? // 15 //

children.text:
na ca dhātvantarārthaṃ yajyādayaḥ pratipādayanti, svārthamātravyāpṛtatvāt |
ataḥ śabdarahitam evedam āropyate bhāvayet iti |
kiñ ca
children.translated_text: For yaj etc. do not convey the meaning of another verbal root, being occupied only with their own meaning. Therefore, [the meaning] 'he should effect' (<s>bhāvayet</s>) is superimposed (<s>āropya</s>) without any corresponding word. Moreover,

children.text: śabdāntarasya yo 'py arthaḥ paryāyair abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Even a meaning of another word that is expressed by synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>)

children.text: na sa tenaiva sahitas tasminn arthe prayujyate // 16 //
children.translated_text: is not employed together with that very [word] in the same meaning-context. // 16 //

children.text:
tad yathā pikam ānaya ity ukte yo nāmārthaṃ na pratipadyate, tasmai kokilaśabdam eva kevalaṃ prayuñjate, na kokilaḥ pikaḥ iti, tathātra yady ākhyātasya karotir ṇyanto vā bhavatiḥ paryāyaḥ, tatas tadarthakathane tanmātram eva prayoktavyam, nākhyātapratyayo 'pi |
na hi tadānīṃ vivicya jñāyate---kenāṃśena kriyā pratyāyyate---iti |
atra tu bhāvayet kuryāt iti vā punar api liṅ prayujyate eva |
ataś ca yo 'nena yajateḥ pareṇārthaḥ pratipāditaḥ, asau bhāvayater api pareṇa tenaivety adhikāvāpa eva bhāvayatiḥ |
tasmād avaidika iti |
atrābhidhīyate |
sarvatraiva tāvat
children.translated_text: For example, when told 'bring the <s>pika</s>,' for one who does not understand the meaning of the word, one uses merely the word <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) alone, not [the sentence] 'a <s>kokila</s> is a <s>pika</s>.' Similarly here, if <s>karoti</s> (to do) or the <s>ṇyanta</s> (causative) <s>bhavati</s> (to become) is a synonym of the <s>ākhyāta</s> (finite verb), then in stating its meaning, that alone should be used, not the verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta-pratyaya</s>) as well. For at that point one cannot discriminately know — 'by which component is the action conveyed?' But here, <s>bhāvayet</s> ('one should bring about') or <s>kuryāt</s> ('one should do') — the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) is indeed employed again. And therefore, whatever meaning has been conveyed by <s>yajati</s> (he sacrifices) through the additional [suffix], that very same [meaning] is conveyed by <s>bhāvayati</s> (he brings about) through the additional [suffix] — thus <s>bhāvayati</s> is merely redundant. Therefore [it follows that bhāvayati] is non-Vedic. To this we reply: In every case, to begin with —

children.text: siddhakartṛkriyāvāciny ākhyātapratyaye sati /
children.translated_text: When a verbal suffix (<s>ākhyāta-pratyaya</s>) expressing an established agent and action is present,

children.text: sāmānādhikaraṇyena karotyartho 'vagamyate // 17 //
children.translated_text: the meaning of <s>karoti</s> (to do) is understood through co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). || 17 ||

children.text:
iha kebhyaścid dhātubhyaḥ parā tiṅvibhaktir uccāryamāṇā kartrātmalābhamātram eva vyāpāraṃ pratipādayati |
yathāstibhavatividyatibhyaḥ |
aparebhyas tu siddhe kartari anyātmalā-
%p. 71
bhaviṣayavyāpārapratītiḥ |
yathā yajati dadāti paṭhati gacchati iti |
dravyam eva ca viśīṣṭaśaktyupetaṃ pracalitātmatattvaṃ viprakīrṇasvabhāvaṃ pūrvāparībhūtaṃ prathamāvasthātaḥ pracyutaṃ parām avasthām aprāptaṃ vyāpāraśabdavācyaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: Here, from certain verbal roots, the <s>tiṅ</s>-inflection, when pronounced after [them], conveys an activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>) that is merely the agent's own self-attainment (<s>ātmalābha</s>) — as from <s>as</s> (to be), <s>bhū</s> (to become), <s>vid</s> (to exist). But from other [roots], when the agent is established, the cognition of activity is directed toward another's attainment — as in <s>yajati</s> (he sacrifices), <s>dadāti</s> (he gives), <s>paṭhati</s> (he recites), <s>gacchati</s> (he goes). And it is a substance (<s>dravya</s>) itself, endowed with a particular capacity, whose own essential nature has been set in motion, whose nature has become dispersed, which has become sequential [in time], which has departed from its former state and has not yet reached its subsequent state — that is denoted by the word 'activity' (<s>vyāpāra</s>).

children.text:
tatra kadācit kartaivaivamavasthaḥ pratīyate |
kadācit siddhe kartary anyaḥ |
tad yadā kartur evaiṣāvasthā bhavati, tadāsau svayam evānyasmād ātmalābham apekṣamāṇaḥ paraniṣpattāv avyāpriyamāṇatvān na karotiśabdavācyatāṃ bhajate |
children.translated_text: In this regard, sometimes the agent itself is cognized as being in this state [of activity]. Sometimes, when the agent is already established, [the activity belongs to] another. Now when this state belongs to the agent itself, then, being itself dependent on another for self-attainment and not being engaged in the accomplishment of another, it does not come to be denoted by the word <s>karoti</s>.

children.text:
yadā tu labdhātmako 'nyatra vyāpriyate, tadā karoti ity evam apadiśyate |
tathā ca kiṃ karoti paṭhati gacchati iti sāmānyaviśeṣarūpeṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyaprayogo dṛśyate |
na tu kiṃ karoti bhavati asti veti prayujyate |
tasmāl labdhātmakakartṛvyāpāravacanāni karotyarthavanty ākhyātāni |
tatra ca kriyamāṇena kenacid avaśyaṃ bhavitavyam |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: But when [the agent], having attained its own being, is engaged in [producing] something else, then it is designated as <s>karoti</s> (he does/makes). And thus the co-referential usage in the form of general and specific is seen: <s>kiṃ karoti? paṭhati, gacchati</s> ('What does he do? He recites, he goes'). But one does not use: <s>kiṃ karoti? bhavati, asti</s> ('What does he do? He exists, he is'). Therefore, verbal forms (<s>ākhyāta</s>) that express the activity of an agent who has attained [its own] being have the meaning of <s>karoti</s>. And in that case, there must necessarily be something that is being made (<s>kriyamāṇa</s>). Why?

children.text: karotiḥ kriyamāṇena na kaścit karmaṇā vinā /
children.translated_text: <s>Karoti</s> (to do/make) [is] never without some object (<s>karma</s>) being made;

children.text: bhavatyarthasya kartā ca karoteḥ karma jāyate // 18 //
children.translated_text: and the agent of <s>bhavati</s> (becoming) becomes the object of <s>karoti</s> (doing). || 18 ||

children.text:
karoter nityaṃ sakarmakatvād yāvat kriyamāṇaṃ na labhyate, na tāvad arthaḥ paryavasyati |
sarvakārakāṇāṃ cāvāntarakriyāsu kartṛtvaṃ pratipādyamānānāṃ pradhānakriyāsu karmādi-
%p. 72
vibhāgo jāyate |
pratikriyaṃ ca yogyatābhedād avāntarakriyāvaicitryaṃ bhavati |
tatrānvayavyatirekābhyām idam avagataṃ bhavatikriyāyāḥ kartā karoteḥ karma saṃpadyate iti |
tathā hi
children.translated_text: Since <s>karoti</s> is invariably transitive (<s>sakarmaka</s>), as long as what is being made is not obtained, the meaning does not come to completion. And all <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations), while being taught as agents with respect to their subsidiary actions, come to be differentiated as objects (<s>karma</s>) etc. in the principal action. And the variety of subsidiary actions differs according to the difference in fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>) for each [principal] action. There, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), this is understood: the agent of the <s>bhavati</s>-action becomes the object of <s>karoti</s>. And thus —

children.text: nityaṃ na bhavanaṃ yasya yasya vā nityabhūtatā /
children.translated_text: That which never comes into being, or that which is eternally existent —

children.text: na tasya kriyamāṇatvaṃ khapuṣpākāśayor iva // 19 //
children.translated_text: for it there is no state of 'being made,' like a sky-flower or space. || 19 ||

children.text:
ya eva hi pravṛttabhavanaḥ saṃbhāvitabhavano vānyena prayujyate, sa eva kriyamāṇatvenāvadhāryate, nānyaḥ |
tathā ca na kaścit khapuṣpam ākāśaṃ vā kurvann upalabhyate |
yatrāpi pādau kuru ityādiṣu niṣpannānāṃ karmaprayogo dṛśyate, tatrāpy aniṣpannasaṃskārādivivakṣayā pādādiśabdaprayogād avyabhicāraḥ |
saty api ca karoter anekārthatve sarvatra gandhanāvakṣepaṇādau kiñcid anutpannotpādanasāmānyam avagamyate |
children.translated_text: For only that which has begun to come into being, or whose coming into being is expected, and which is employed by another — only that is determined as 'being made' (<s>kriyamāṇa</s>), not anything else. And thus no one is observed making a sky-flower or space. Even where the usage of the object is seen with already accomplished [entities], as in <s>pādau kuru</s> ('make [use of your] feet') and the like, there too, because of the intention to express an unaccomplished configuration etc., through the use of the word <s>pāda</s> etc., there is no deviation [from the rule]. And even though <s>karoti</s> has multiple meanings, everywhere — in the application of fragrance, the throwing of a ball, etc. — some general sense of 'producing what has not yet arisen' is understood.

children.text:
atha vā yadāsyotpādanābhidhāyitvam, tadaiva viśiṣṭākhyātasāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ dṛṣṭam iti tadgatasyotpādyamānam eva karma bhavatīty upapannam |
tena bhavatikriyā tāval labdhā |
tataś ca
children.translated_text: Alternatively, precisely when [<s>karoti</s>] has the function of denoting production, then the co-reference with specific verbal forms is observed — thus it is established that the object of that [production] is indeed what is being produced. By this, the <s>bhavati</s>-action (becoming) is obtained. And therefore —

children.text: karotyarthasya yaḥ kartā bhavituḥ sa prayojakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The agent of the <s>karoti</s>-meaning (doing) is the instigator (<s>prayojaka</s>) of <s>bhavati</s> (becoming);

children.text: bhavitā tam apekṣyātha prayojyatvaṃ prapadyate // 20 //
children.translated_text: <s>bhavati</s> (the becomer), depending on that [instigator], then attains the status of the instigated (<s>prayojya</s>). || 20 ||

children.text:
%p. 73
bhavatikarotyoḥ śaktibhedād viklidipacatyor iva niyataṃ prayojyaprayojakavyāpāravacanatvam |
tatra ca (1) kadācid abhidhīyamānakarmaśaktyākṣiptaprayojyavyāpāro vā svayam evākṣiptaprayojyavyāpāro vā kevalaṃ prayojakavyāpāra eva vivakṣyate kaṭaṃ karoti odanaṃ pacati iti |
(2) kadācid ākṣiptaprayojakavyāpāraṃ prayojyavyāpāramātram ghaṭo bhavati viklidyanti taṇḍulāḥ iti |
(3) kadācid ubhau bhinnau samuccitya prayogaḥ karoti kaṭaṃ devadattaḥ, sa ca bhavati iti |
(4) kadācid upasarjanībhūtaprayojakavyāpāraḥ prayojyavyāpāraḥ kriyate devadattena iti, svayam eveti vā prayoge |
(5) kadācit punaḥ samānapadaikadeśopāttopasarjanībhūtaprayojyakriyaḥ prayojakavyāpāro vivakṣyate, tadā ca karotipacatyos tādātmyenāśakter arprayogāt, bhūviklidyoś ca kevalaprayojyakriyāniṣṭhatvān na sākṣāt pravartituṃ śaktir astīti vācakatvena dyotakatvena vā ṇicparaḥ prayujyate bhāvayati vikledayati iti ca |
tathā cāha---
children.translated_text: Due to the difference in capacity between <s>bhavati</s> and <s>karoti</s>, just as between <s>viklid</s> (to melt) and <s>pac</s> (to cook), there is necessarily the denotation of instigated and instigating activity (<s>prayojya-prayojaka-vyāpāra</s>). And in this regard: (1) Sometimes only the instigating activity is intended, with the instigated activity being implied by the capacity of the stated object or implied on its own — as in <s>kaṭaṃ karoti</s> ('he makes a mat'), <s>odanaṃ pacati</s> ('he cooks rice'). (2) Sometimes only the instigated activity is expressed, with the instigating activity implied — as in <s>ghaṭo bhavati</s> ('the pot comes into being'), <s>viklidyanti taṇḍulāḥ</s> ('the grains soften'). (3) Sometimes both are combined separately in usage — as in <s>karoti kaṭaṃ Devadattaḥ, sa ca bhavati</s> ('<s>Devadatta</s> makes the mat, and it comes into being'). (4) Sometimes the instigated activity is expressed with the instigating activity subordinated — as in <s>kriyate Devadattena</s> ('it is made by <s>Devadatta</s>') or <s>svayam eva</s> ('by itself'). (5) Sometimes, when the instigating activity is intended with the instigated action subordinated and taken up as part of the same word-form, then — since <s>karoti</s> and <s>pacati</s> cannot be used due to lack of identity [with the subordinate meaning], and since <s>bhū</s> and <s>viklid</s>, being exclusively of instigated action, cannot directly function [as the main predicate] — the causative suffix <s>ṇic</s> is employed, either as denotative or as indicative: <s>bhāvayati</s> ('he causes to become'), <s>vikledayati</s> ('he causes to soften'). And accordingly he states —

children.text: prayojyakartṛkaikāntavyāpārapratipādakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>ṇyanta</s> (causative) forms are employed precisely for the expression of activity whose agent is exclusively the instigated party (<s>prayojya</s>),

children.text: ṇyantā eva prayujyante tatprayojakakarmasu // 21 //
children.translated_text: [namely] when [the instigators] serve as the objects of those instigators (<s>prayojaka</s>). || 21 ||

children.text:
na ca teṣām aṇyantānām aśaktir ity anyeṣām aśaktyā bhavitavyam, anyeṣāṃ vā śaktir ity eṣām api tathā bhavitavyam |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And it should not be [argued] that because those [causative forms] are incapable, others too must be incapable; or that because others are capable, these too must be likewise. Why?

children.text: śaktayaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ nānuyojyāḥ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The capacities (<s>śakti</s>) of all entities are not to be questioned as to their nature;

children.text: tena nānā vadanty arthān prakṛtipratyayādayaḥ // 22 //
children.translated_text: therefore roots, suffixes, and the like express different meanings. || 22 ||

children.text:
%p. 74
evaṃ karotyarthadvāreṇa sarvākhyāteṣu bhāvayatyarthaḥ siddhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, through the medium of the <s>karoti</s>-meaning, the meaning of <s>bhāvayati</s> (causation/productive operation) is established in all verbal forms.

children.text: tena bhūtiṣu kartṛtvaṃ pratipannasya vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the productive activity (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of an entity that has attained agency in states of becoming —

children.text: prayojakakriyām āhur bhāvanāṃ bhāvanāvidaḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: those who understand <s>bhāvanā</s> call [this] the instigating action. || 23 ||

children.text:
yat tūktaṃ na vidhivyatiriktaṃ liṅādayo 'rthaṃ vadantīti, tad ayuktam |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: As for the objection that the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) etc. do not express a meaning beyond injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) — that is incorrect. Why?

children.text: abhidhābhāvanām āhur anyām eva liṅādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The optative (<s>liṅ</s>) etc. express one kind of <s>bhāvanā</s>, namely that of verbal expression (<s>abhidhā-bhāvanā</s>);

children.text: arthātmabhāvanā tv anyā sarvākhyāteṣu gamyate // 24 //
children.translated_text: but another <s>bhāvanā</s>, that pertaining to the thing itself (<s>arthātma-bhāvanā</s>), is understood in all verbal forms. || 24 ||

children.text:
yadā hi sarvākhyātānuvartinī karotidhātuvācyā puruṣavyāpārarūpā bhāvanāvagatā bhavati, tadā tadviśeṣāḥ sāmānyākhyātavyatiriktaśabdaviśeṣavācyā vidhipratiṣedhabhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānādayaḥ pratīyante |
tathā ca sarvatra sāmānyataḥ karotyartho 'vagamyate, kiṃ karoti? pacati, kim akārṣīt? apākṣīt, kiṃ kariṣyati? pakṣyati, kiṃ kuryāt? pacet, kiṃ na kuryāt? na pacet iti |
tatrārthātmikāyāṃ bhāvanāyāṃ liṅādiśabdānāṃ yaḥ puruṣaṃ prati prayojakavyāpāraḥ, sā dvitīyā śabdadharmo 'bhidhātmikā bhāvanā vi-
%p. 75
dhir ity ucyate |
viśeṣataś ceyam arthavādādhikaraṇe varṇitā |
yat tu paryāyasthityatilaṅghanaṃ pratyayāparityāgād abhihitam, tatrocyate---
children.translated_text: For when the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) denoted by the root <s>kṛ</s> (to do), which pervades all verbal forms and has the nature of human activity (<s>puruṣa-vyāpāra</s>), is understood, then its particular forms — injunction, prohibition, past, present, etc. — are cognized as expressed by specific words distinct from the general verbal form. And thus, in every case the <s>karoti</s>-meaning is understood in a general way: <s>kiṃ karoti? pacati</s> ('What does he do? He cooks'); <s>kim akārṣīt? apākṣīt</s> ('What did he do? He cooked'); <s>kiṃ kariṣyati? pakṣyati</s> ('What will he do? He will cook'); <s>kiṃ kuryāt? pacet</s> ('What should he do? He should cook'); <s>kiṃ na kuryāt? na pacet</s> ('What should he not do? He should not cook'). There, with respect to the <s>bhāvanā</s> pertaining to the thing itself (<s>arthātmikā bhāvanā</s>), that instigating activity of the optative (<s>liṅ</s>) etc. toward the person — that second [<s>bhāvanā</s>], a property of the word, pertaining to verbal expression (<s>abhidhātmikā</s>), is called injunction (<s>vidhi</s>). This has been discussed in detail in the <s>arthavāda</s> section. Now, regarding the objection about not abandoning the suffix when transgressing the order of synonyms, we say —

children.text: kevalasyāprayogitvāt kartṛsaṃkhyādisaṃgrahāt /
children.translated_text: Because the bare [root] cannot be used alone, because of the inclusion of agent-number etc.,

children.text: rūpāvināśasiddheś ca pratyayo 'pi prayujyate // 25 //
children.translated_text: and because the established form is not destroyed — the suffix too is employed. || 25 ||

children.text:
yadi hi kevalaḥ karotir bhāvayatir vā prayogārhau syātām, tataḥ kokilaśabdaprayoge pikaśabdavat pratyayo na prayujyeta |
na tu kevalāyāḥ prakṛteḥ prayogaḥ |
apabhraṃśatvaprasaṅgāt |
tena yasmin kasmiṃścit pratyaye prayoktavye yasyaivārthaḥ kathyate, sa evānuvādabhūtaḥ prakṛtyanugrahārthaṃ prayujyate, nānyaḥ |
abhyadhikārthāntarāpattiprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: For if the bare root <s>karoti</s> or <s>bhāvayati</s> were fit for usage [alone], then, just as the word <s>pika</s> [is not needed] when the word <s>kokila</s> is used, the suffix would not be employed. But a bare root (<s>prakṛti</s>) cannot be used [alone], because it would amount to a corrupt form (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>). Therefore, when any suffix must be employed, only that [suffix] whose meaning is being stated is employed in a reiterated capacity for the purpose of supporting the root — not another. Because [using another] would lead to the undesirable consequence of [introducing] an additional, extraneous meaning.

children.text:
nanu ca ikśtipau dhātunirdeśe vihitāu, atas tadyuktau karotibhāvayatī prayjyeyātām |
naitad asti |
tathā sati śabdapadārthakatvān naiva tābhyām ākhyātārthaḥ kathyeta |
children.translated_text: But [the objector says:] since <s>ikṣ</s> and <s>tipau</s> are prescribed in the enumeration of roots (<s>dhātunirdeśa</s>), therefore <s>karoti</s> and <s>bhāvayati</s>, equipped with those, should be employed. This is not so. In that case, since they would be [mere] word-referents, the meaning of the verbal form (<s>ākhyātārtha</s>) would not at all be expressed by them.

children.text:
yat tu kvacid arthe 'pi dhātum ikśtibantaṃ prayuñjate yajiḥ yajatiḥ iti, tac chabde 'bhihite lakṣaṇayārthapratītir ity avagantavyaṃ |
na ceha kiṃcil lakṣa-
%p. 76
ṇāśrayaṇe prayojanam asti yenāvācakaḥ prayujyeta |
tatrānyad evāniṣṭam āpadyeta kṛñbhuvau dhātū tiṅābhidhīyete iti |
tasmād arthaparatvasiddhyartham ākhyātapratyayasahitāv eva prayujyete |
children.translated_text: Now, as for the fact that sometimes even for an object-meaning (artha) they employ a root with the suffix -ikṣti, such as 'yajiḥ' and 'yajatiḥ' — it should be understood that when the word [itself] is already expressed, the cognition of the object-meaning is through lakṣaṇā (secondary signification). And here there is no purpose in resorting to secondary signification by which a non-denotative [word] would be employed. In that case, a different undesirable consequence would follow — [namely] that 'kṛñ and bhū, these two roots, are denoted by the tiṅ [suffixes].' Therefore, for the purpose of establishing the primacy of the object-meaning, they are employed only together with the <s>ākhyāta</s> (verbal) suffixes.

children.text:
yadi ca bhāvanaivaikā pratyayārthaḥ syāt karotibhāvayatī vā samastapratyayārthopādānasamarthau bhavetām, tataḥ kevalaprayogo 'py āśaṅkyeta, na tu tad ubhayam apy astīti karotibhāvayatibhyāṃ kathite 'pi bhāvanārthe kartṛsaṃkhyādipratyāyanārthaṃ punaḥ pratyaya uccāryate |
yas tu tatra bhāvanābhidhānāṃśaḥ sa prāptatvād anūdyate. anyathā hi bhāvanaivaikā pratyayārthaḥ karotibhāvayatī vā kartṛsaṃkhyādīnām apy abhidhāyakāv iti bhrāntiḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: And if <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive activity) alone were the meaning of the suffix, then 'karoti' (he does) or 'bhāvayati' (he brings into being) would be capable of conveying the entire suffix-meaning, and then even a use [of the root] alone might be suspected. But since neither of these two [conditions] obtains, even when the meaning of <s>bhāvanā</s> has been expressed by 'karoti' or 'bhāvayati,' the suffix is again uttered for the purpose of conveying the agent, number, etc. The portion that [merely] expresses <s>bhāvanā</s> in those [forms] is [merely] restated (<s>anūdita</s>), since it has already been obtained. Otherwise, there would be the confusion that <s>bhāvanā</s> alone is the suffix-meaning, or that 'karoti' and 'bhāvayati' also denote agent, number, etc.

children.text:
nityaṃ ca pūrvāparībhūtā bhāvanākhyātenocyate |
tatra yadi pratyayāntaraṃ prayujyeta, tataḥ karotibhāvayatibhyāṃ dravyavad upasaṃhṛtarūpocyamānā naivākhyātasadṛśī kathyeta |
tasmād avaśyaṃ tiṅ api prayoktavya iti |
children.translated_text: And invariably, <s>bhāvanā</s>, as something that has [the character of] before and after (i.e., a process), is expressed by the <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb). If another suffix were employed there, then [<s>bhāvanā</s>], being expressed as having a completed form subsumed like a substance — through 'karoti' or 'bhāvayati' — would not be described as resembling an <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb). Therefore, the <s>tiṅ</s> [suffix] too must necessarily be employed.

children.text:
%p. 77
kiñ ca---
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: bhāvanā gamyamānā ca dhātupratyayasaṃnidhau /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāvanā</s> (productive activity), when cognized in the proximity of root and suffix,

children.text: kasya vācyeti vispaṣṭaṃ na kadācit pratīyate // 26 //
children.translated_text: is never clearly understood as 'whose denotation [is it]?' // 26 //

children.text:
yadi hy ekāntenāsyāḥ pratyayārthatvam avadhāryeta, tataḥ karotibhāvayatibhyāṃ pratyayapaunaruktyāśaṅkā syān, na tu tad asti |
ubhayasannidhau gamyamānatvāt |
kevalaprakṛtipratyayaprayogābhāvād dhi na viveko vijñāyate |
śakyate hi vaktuṃ dhātusahitena pratyayenocyata iti,
atha vā pratyayānugṛhītena dhātunā, atha vobhābhyām |
na ca śaktikalpanāyāṃ viśeṣaḥ |
sarvathārthāpattisāmyāt |
na ca vivekajñānaprayojanam asti |
children.translated_text: For if its being the suffix-meaning were determined with certainty, then there would be the suspicion of redundancy of the suffix with [the forms] 'karoti' and 'bhāvayati.' But that is not the case, because [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is cognized in the proximity of both [root and suffix]. Since there is no occurrence of root or suffix being employed alone, the distinction is not discerned. For it can be said that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is expressed by the suffix together with the root, or alternatively, by the root assisted by the suffix, or else by both together. And there is no difference in the postulation of [denotative] power, since <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is equal in all cases. Nor is there any purpose served by knowing the distinction.

children.text:
syād etat |
kṛdantād dhātor apratītes tiṅvyabhicāriṇy eva bhāvaneti |
tad ayuktam |
astibhavatividyatipareṣu pratyayeṣv apy adarśanāt |
na ca kṛdanteṣv apy atyantaṃ bhāvanā nāsti |
kiṃcid apakṛṣyamāṇarūparpatīteḥ |
(1) kṛtyeṣu tāvad bhoktavyam yaṣṭavyam iti kiṃcin nyūnākhyātād gamyate |
tatrāpi karmotpanneṣu dravyaprādhānyād brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ iti bhāvotpannebhyo nyūnatarā |
na hi tatra prayojakavyāpāraprādhānyam |
ekatra dhātvarthaprādhānyāt, aparatra svavyāpāraviśiṣṭaprayojyaparatvāt |
etena bhāvakarmotpannalakārās tiṅo 'pi vyākhyātāḥ |
teṣv api hi prayojakavyāpāraguṇatvapratītir aviśiṣṭā |
ato na tiṅantānāṃ tulyakalpatvam |
%p. 78
(2) tathā avyayakṛto bhāve bhavanti iti smaraṇāviśeṣe 'pi svasaṃvedyam īṣannyūnabhāvanāvijñānam |
abhikrāmaṃ juhoti, darbhataruṇakenopaghātaṃ juhoti, abhiṣutya hutvā bhakṣayanti, purā vācaḥ pravaditoḥ iti sarvatra śrutyaiva bhāvanāntarasāpekṣā bhāvanāvagamyate |
(3) pakvaḥ pakvavān ity api nirvṛttarūpabhāvanopasarjanadravyapratītiḥ pratyakṣā |
(4) evaṃ pācakādiṣv api draṣṭavyam |
tathā ca sarvatra kārakāpekṣā dṛśyate |
anyathā hi rūḍhitaddhitasamāseṣv iveyaṃ na syāt |
na ca nirvyāpārāṇām ete vyapadeśā bhavanti |
na cāsti sa vyāpāro yatra kiṃcid asan na janyate |
tataś ca siddhaḥ karotibhāvayatyor arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: It may be objected: since <s>bhāvanā</s> is not cognized from a root in a <s>kṛt</s> (primary nominal) derivative, <s>bhāvanā</s> is invariably concomitant with <s>tiṅ</s> [suffixes] alone. That is not correct, because [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is not seen even in suffixes after 'asti' (exists), 'bhavati' (becomes), and 'vidyati' (is found). Nor is <s>bhāvanā</s> entirely absent in <s>kṛt</s> derivatives, because there is cognition of a somewhat diminished form [of it]. (1) In <s>kṛtya</s> (gerundive) forms, at least, such as 'bhoktavyam' (should be eaten), 'yaṣṭavyam' (should be sacrificed), something is cognized that falls slightly short of a [full] verb. Among those too, the ones derived from <s>karma</s> (object), due to the predominance of the substance, [as in] 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed,' are inferior [in expressing <s>bhāvanā</s>] compared to those derived from <s>bhāva</s> (action). For in those, the predominance of the instigator's activity is not [prominent] — in one case due to the predominance of the root-meaning, in the other due to the predominance of the object (thing acted upon) qualified by its own activity. By this, the <s>lakāras</s> (verbal tenses/moods) derived from <s>bhāva</s> and <s>karma</s> among the <s>tiṅ</s> [suffixes] are also explained — for in those too, the cognition of the subordinate nature of the instigator's activity is no different. Therefore, [all forms ending in] <s>tiṅ</s> are not of equal status. (2) Likewise, although in the case of the <s>avyaya-kṛt</s> (indeclinable participle) forms, there is [the rule] 'they occur in the sense of bhāva,' and despite no difference in the statement, the cognition of a slightly diminished <s>bhāvanā</s> is self-evident. [In examples such as] 'having approached, he offers,' 'he offers with a blow using fresh darbha grass,' 'having pressed the soma, having offered, they eat,' 'before the utterance of speech' — in all cases, <s>bhāvanā</s> is understood through the Vedic text itself as dependent on another <s>bhāvanā</s>. (3) In [forms like] 'pakvaḥ' (cooked) and 'pakvavān' (one who has cooked), the cognition of a substance subordinate to a <s>bhāvanā</s> of completed form is directly evident. (4) The same should be observed in [agent nouns like] 'pācaka' (cook) etc. And thus in all cases, dependence on <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) is observed. Otherwise, this [dependence] would not exist, as in the case of <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional) words, <s>taddhita</s> (secondary) derivatives, and compounds. And these designations do not apply to things devoid of activity. Nor is there any activity in which something non-existent is not produced. Therefore, the meaning of 'karoti' and 'bhāvayati' is established.

children.text:
śakyate ca sarvatra sāmānādhikaraṇyam api darśayituṃ vināpi pūrvāparībhūtatvena |
tad yathā kiṃ kartavyaṃ? paktavyam, kathaṃkāraṃ juhoti? abhikrāmam, kiṃ kṛtvā juhoti? abhiṣutya, kiṃ kṛtavān? pakvavān, kiṃ
%p. 79
kṛtam? pakvaṃ, kiṃkriyo devadattaḥ? paktā, keyaṃ kriyā? pākaḥ iti |
na ca karotisāmānādhikaraṇyātiriktam ākhyāteṣv api bhāvanāpramāṇaṃ vidyate |
tasmād dhātavo 'pi bhāvanāṃ na muñcanti |
tathā cāhuḥ karotir artheṣv iva sarvadhātūn iti |
yat tv asyāḥ prādhānyaṃ tat kāmaṃ tiṅābhidheyaṃ dyotyaṃ vānvayavyatirekābhyām astu, na svarūpam |
children.translated_text: And it is possible to show the co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) everywhere, even without [the criterion of] being prior-and-posterior. For example: 'What is to be done (kartavya)? It is to be cooked (paktavya).' 'How does he offer? By approaching.' 'Having done what, does he offer? Having pressed the soma.' 'What has he done? He has cooked.' 'What has been done? [It is] cooked.' 'What is <s>Devadatta</s> doing? He is a cook.' 'What is this action? Cooking.' And there is no evidence for <s>bhāvanā</s> in verbs (<s>ākhyātas</s>) beyond the co-referentiality with 'karoti.' Therefore, even roots do not abandon <s>bhāvanā</s>. And thus they say: 'karoti [applies to] all roots just as [it applies to] objects.' As for the predominance of [<s>bhāvanā</s>], let that be denoted or indicated by the <s>tiṅ</s> [suffix] through positive and negative concomitance — but not its essential nature.

children.text:
nanv evam api yāgena iti dhātvarthe niṣkṛṣṭe tenaiva bhāvanāpy upātteti bhāvayet iti punaḥ prayogo na prāpnoti |
naiṣa doṣaḥ |
tathā hi dvyarthasya dhātor bhedenārthe kathyamāne yāgena iti viśeṣarūpaṃ karaṇātmanā niṣkṛṣṭam |
itarat tu bhāvanātmakaṃ sāmānyarūpaṃ śabdāntareṇa bhāvayet ity anena kathyate |
children.translated_text: Objection: Even so, when the root-meaning has been extracted by [the instrumental case in] 'yāgena' (by the sacrifice), <s>bhāvanā</s> too has been included through that very [extraction], so the further use of 'bhāvayet' (one should bring about) would not be warranted. This is not a fault. For when the two-fold meaning of the root is separately stated, the specific form [of the meaning] has been extracted in the form of the instrument by 'yāgena.' The other [meaning], which has the nature of <s>bhāvanā</s>, being a general form, is expressed by a different word, namely 'bhāvayet.'

children.text:
atha vā kecit karaṇāṃśakartṛsaṃkhyādayaḥ prakṛtipratyayayor bhedena vācyāḥ |
bhāvanā tu samudāyāvyabhicārāt samucitayor evārtha ity api śakyaṃ vaktum |
tathā ca sūtrakārabhāṣyakārābhyāṃ bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdāḥ iti sāmānādhikaraṇyam evāśritam, na bhāvārthatvena pratyayāḥ kathitāḥ |
śāstre tu sarvatra pratyayārtho bhāvaneti vyavahāraḥ |
tatrāyam abhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, certain [aspects] — the instrument-portion, agent, number, etc. — are to be expressed separately by root and suffix [respectively]. But <s>bhāvanā</s>, because it invariably accompanies the combination [of root and suffix], can also be said to be the meaning of both taken together. And thus the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (<s>Jaimini</s>) and the <s>bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śabara</s>) have relied on the co-referentiality [expressed by the statement] 'bhāvārthāḥ karmaśabdāḥ' (action-words have the sense of bhāva), and have not declared the suffixes as having the meaning of bhāva. But in the <s>śāstra</s> (science of grammar), everywhere the convention is that 'the suffix-meaning is <s>bhāvanā</s>.' The intention there is as follows:

children.text: pratyayārthaṃ saha brūtaḥ prakṛtipratyayau sadā /
children.translated_text: Root and suffix always express the suffix-meaning together.

children.text: prādhānyād bhāvanā tena pratyayārtho 'vadhāryate // 27 //
children.translated_text: Because of [its] predominance, <s>bhāvanā</s> is thereby determined to be the suffix-meaning. // 27 //

children.text: yady apy anyad vivekakāraṇaṃ nāsti, tathāpi prādhānyaṃ pratyayārthadharmaṃ dṛṣṭvā nūnam iyaṃ pratyayārthaḥ ity avagamyate |
children.translated_text: Even though there is no other means of distinguishing, nevertheless, seeing that predominance is a property of the suffix-meaning, it is understood that 'surely this [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is the suffix-meaning.'

children.text: tathā kramavator nityaṃ prakṛtipratyayāśayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, since root and suffix always have a sequential order,

children.text: pratyayaśrutivelāyāṃ bhāvanātmāvagamyate // 28 //
children.translated_text: at the moment of hearing the suffix, the essence of <s>bhāvanā</s> is cognized. // 28 //

children.text:
na kevalam etāv evānvayavyatirekau yau parasparaparityāgena lakṣyete |
tasminn eva hi pade tadāgame hi tad dṛśyate ity anena nyāyena viveko 'vadhāryate |
children.translated_text: Not only are these the [criteria of] positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>) that are observed through mutual exclusion. Rather, within that very word, the distinction is determined by the principle that 'upon the arrival of that [element], that [meaning] is observed.'

children.text:
yat tv astyādiparaḥ pratyayo 'pi bhāvanāṃ jahātīti tulyaṃ dhātusamudāyapakṣayor apy etat |
sarvathā yatra pratīyate, tatra tāvat pratyayārthatvaṃ niścīyate |
anyatra tv ayaṃ vicāra eva nāsti |
kvacid vyabhicārasya cottaram uktaṃ tadbhūtādhikaraṇe |
atha vā naivātrāpi vyabhicāraḥ |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: As for [the objection] that the suffix after 'asti' etc. also abandons <s>bhāvanā</s> — this [objection] applies equally to both the suffix-position and the root-combination-position. In any case, wherever [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is cognized, there its being the suffix-meaning is ascertained. But elsewhere, this inquiry simply does not arise. And the response to the occasional deviation has been stated in the <s>tadbhūtādhikaraṇa</s> (the section on 'becoming that'). Alternatively, there is indeed no deviation here at all. Why?

children.text: astyādāv api kartraṃśe bhāvye 'sty eva hi bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Even in [verbs like] 'asti' etc., with respect to the agent-portion, there is indeed <s>bhāvanā</s> in what is to be brought into being.

children.text: anyatrāśeṣabhāvāt tu na tathā sā prakāśate // 29 //
children.translated_text: But since elsewhere [the brought-into-being] is exhausted by [mere] existence, [<s>bhāvanā</s>] does not manifest in the same way. // 29 //

children.text:
yady api kartur aniṣpannatvād vyatiriktabhāvayitavyābhāvād astyādiṣu prayojakavyāpāro nātīva lakṣyate, tathāpi pratyayasāmarthyāt tāvat bhāvayati ity avagamyate |
kim? ity apekṣite cāniṣpanne kartari anyat kiṃcit ity akalpanād ātmānam ity eva saṃbadhayte |
kena? bhāvanena, katham? avayavajananādirpakāreṇa iti |
trayo 'pi tatra bhāvanāṃśā bhavanenaiva pūryante. vyāpārāntarāsaṃbhavāt |
tatra kecid avayavā bhavanavyāprtāḥ prayujyante, kecit siddhabhavanāḥ prayojakāḥ |
siddhabhavanāsiddhabhavanavarti ca sāmānyam ubhayasaṃparkād bhāvanety ucyate |
etena jāyate niṣpadyate sidhyati ityādīni vyākhyātāni |
children.translated_text: Although in [verbs like] 'asti' etc., since the agent is already accomplished and there is no separate thing to be brought into being, the instigator's activity is not very prominent — nevertheless, at least by the force of the suffix, 'bhāvayati' (he brings into being) is understood. When the question 'what?' arises, since the agent is already accomplished, and since there is no [reason to] postulate anything else [as the object], 'himself' alone is connected [as the answer]. 'By what?' By existence (<s>bhavana</s>). 'How?' Through the process of generating limbs/parts, etc. All three aspects of <s>bhāvanā</s> are fulfilled there by existence (<s>bhavana</s>) alone, due to the impossibility of any other activity. Among those, certain limbs/parts are employed while engaged in the activity of existence; others, having completed existence, are the instigators. And the universal that pervades both the state of completed existence and uncompleted existence is called <s>bhāvanā</s>, due to its connection with both. By this, [verbs like] 'jāyate' (is born), 'niṣpadyate' (is accomplished), 'sidhyati' (succeeds), etc. are explained.

children.text:
astiḥ punar janisamānārthād bhavater uparitanīm avasthām abhilapan sattayātmabhavanaṃ bhavad bhāvayatīty evam ākhyātapratyayaṃ labhate |
tatrāpi tu kālakṛtabhedapūrvottarasāmānyasattārūpeṇa pūrvavad eva prayojyaprayojakavyāpārakalpanānusartavyā |
children.translated_text: 'Asti' (exists), however, expressing the higher state than 'bhavati' (becomes) — which is synonymous with 'jani' (birth) — [denotes that] the existing [entity] 'brings into being' (bhāvayati) its own existence (<s>ātmabhavana</s>), and thus it obtains the <s>ākhyāta</s> (verbal) suffix. But even there, the postulation of the activity of the caused and the causer, in the form of the general existence [comprising] prior and posterior [states] differentiated by time, should be followed just as before.

children.text:
satyām api tv evamādiṣu bhāvanāyāṃ niṣpannacetanakartṛviṣayatvād vidhipratiṣedhayor asaṃbhavaḥ |
syād etat |
dṛṣṭo vidhir api tasmāt prāyaṇīyasyāhna ṛtvijā bhavi-
%p. 82
tavyam, rathaṃtaraṃ bhavati, atrādhvaryuḥ syāt, ihokthyāni syuḥ iti |
satyaṃ dṛśyate, na tv iha pūrveṇa tulyo bhavatyarthaḥ |
siddho hi puruṣaḥ karmasaṃbandhanimittam ṛtviktvaṃ bhavad anyair eva parikrayaṇādibhir vyāpārair bhāvayed ity ucyate |
tathā rathaṃtarādiṣu saty api śrutyā bhavanavidhisaṃbandhe tatrāsaṃbhavād anumīyamānā bhāvanaiva vidhīyate |
yatra tu ihāmuko bhavet iti prayogas tatra bhavates tiṣṭhatyarthavācitvāt saṃbhavaty eva vyatiriktaṃ bhāvayitavyam ity evaṃ vijñāyate sthānenānyat kiṃcid bhāvayet iti |
children.translated_text: However, even though there is <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive activity) in such [usages], since injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) and prohibition (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) have as their domain a conscious agent who has already come into being [as the performer], [the application of <s>bhāvanā</s> in those cases] is impossible. One might say: Injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is indeed observed [with the verb <s>bhavati</s>], as in: 'The <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest) should be [present] on the day of the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> [offering]'; '<s>Rathantara</s> [<s>sāman</s>] is [to be used]'; 'Here the <s>Adhvaryu</s> should be'; 'Here the <s>Ukthya</s> [offerings] should be.' [p. 82] True, [such usage] is observed; but the meaning here is not equivalent to the former [i.e., <s>bhāvanā</s> in the technical sense]. For the person [i.e., the priest] is already established, and the state of being an <s>ṛtvij</s> — which is the ground for [his] connection with the ritual action — is said to be brought about (<s>bhāvayet</s>) through other activities such as hiring and the like. Likewise, in the case of <s>Rathantara</s> and the like, even though there is a connection of the injunction to bring about [something] with scripture, since that [direct bringing about] is impossible there, it is the inferred <s>bhāvanā</s> itself that is enjoined. But where the usage is 'let so-and-so be here,' since <s>bhavati</s> ('is') has the meaning of standing/existing, it is indeed possible [to understand] that something distinct is to be brought about — i.e., it is understood as: 'Let him bring about something else by [his] standing [there].'

children.text:
tena bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānāpadeśamātreṣv evāpāramārthikaṃ bhavitṛvyāpārasya bhāvanātvam, na vidhyādiṣu |
bhūtādikathane 'pi yadā samastaṃ vyāpāraṃ dhātur evopādatte nāvayavakālādikṛtabhedāśrayaṇam, tadā vispaṣṭād virodhād dhātvarthamātram |
kartṛsaṃkhyādayaś cākhyātapadārthatvenāvadhāryante, na bhāvanā |
na ca bhāvanāvyabhicāreṇa doṣa ity uktam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the character of the agent's activity as <s>bhāvanā</s> applies only figuratively in expressions that merely indicate past, future, and present tenses, not in injunctions (<s>vidhi</s>) and the like. Even in past-tense narration and the like, when the verbal root takes up the entire activity without recourse to the distinction based on parts, time, etc., then, due to the clear contradiction, it [denotes] merely the meaning of the verbal root. And the agent, number, and the like are apprehended as the meaning of the verbal ending (<s>ākhyāta-pada</s>), not as <s>bhāvanā</s>. And it has been stated that there is no fault in the invariable concomitance with <s>bhāvanā</s>.

children.text:
yat tu kṛdanteṣv api dhātavo bhāvanāṃ na vyabhicarantīti |
satyaṃ dhātvarthā na vyabhicaranti |
tair eva tu gamyamānatvād anabhidheyatvam api śakyaṃ vaktum |
tathā hi
children.translated_text: As for [the objection] that even in verbal derivatives (<s>kṛdanta</s>), verbal roots do not deviate from [denoting] <s>bhāvanā</s> — true, the meanings of the verbal roots do not deviate. But since they are understood through those very [roots], it is also possible to say that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is not [separately] expressed. For thus:

children.text: dhātvarthakārakair eva guṇabhūto 'vagamyate /
children.translated_text: In verbal derivatives (<s>kṛdanta</s>), [<s>bhāvanā</s>] — being of the nature of productive activity — is understood as a subordinate [element] only through the meaning of the verbal root and the <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations);

children.text: bhāvanātmā kṛdanteṣu tasmān naivābhidhīyate // 30 //
children.translated_text: therefore, it is not [separately] expressed [by the <s>kṛdanta</s> form]. // 30 //

children.text:
yathaiva bhāvapradhānatvād ākhyāte tatsambandhād eva guṇabhūtakārakarpratītishiddher na kartṛkarmaṇor abhidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati, evaṃ kartrādyabhidhānād eva tadanyathānupapattyā bhāvanāsiddher anabhidhānam |
