gamyamānāpekṣayaiva ca karotisāmānādhikaraṇyam, yathā pacatiśabdasya devadattaśabdena |
tathābhūtayaiva ca kārakasambandho 'py upapatsyate |
children.translated_text: Just as in the finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>), due to the predominance of the state of being (<s>bhāva</s>), the cognition of the <s>kārakas</s> (agent, object, etc.) is established only through their connection with it, and therefore the agent and object will not be [separately] expressed [by the verb]; similarly, from the very expression of the agent and the like, since <s>bhāvanā</s> is established through the impossibility of [the activity] being otherwise — it is not [separately] expressed. And the co-referentiality with <s>karoti</s> ('does') is merely with respect to what is understood [by implication], just as [the co-referentiality] of the word <s>pacati</s> ('cooks') with the word <s>Devadatta</s>. And the connection with the <s>kārakas</s> will also be explained by [<s>bhāvanā</s>] being of just such a nature.

children.text:
atha vā bhāvanopasarjanadhātvarthaniṣpattyarthatvāt kārakāṇāṃ dhātvarthenaiva saṃbandhasiddhiḥ |
sa eva hi tāni svasiddhyartham apekṣate |
bhāvanāpi ca tathābhūtāny eva tāni gṛhṇātīty aviruddhaḥ sambandhaḥ |
kṛtyānāṃ tu praiṣavācitvāt saty api bhāvanānabhidhāne tāvat svārthaparyavasānaṃ nāsti yāvad aṃśatrayaparipūrṇā bhāvanā na labdhā |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, since the <s>kārakas</s> serve the purpose of accomplishing the meaning of the verbal root — which is subordinate to <s>bhāvanā</s> — their connection is established through the meaning of the verbal root itself. For it is that [verbal root meaning] alone that requires them for its own accomplishment. And <s>bhāvanā</s> too grasps them only as having such a nature — hence the connection is not contradictory. But in the case of <s>kṛtya</s> forms [verbal adjectives of obligation], since they express a command (<s>praiṣa</s>), even though <s>bhāvanā</s> is not [directly] expressed, there is no termination of their own meaning until <s>bhāvanā</s> — complete with its three aspects (<s>aṃśa-traya</s>) — is obtained. Why?

children.text: svavyāpāre hi puruṣaḥ kartṛtvena niyujyate /
children.translated_text: For a person is enjoined as the agent with respect to his own activity;

children.text: praiṣais tasya ca kiṃ karma bhāvanāṃśatrayātmikā // 31 //
children.translated_text: and what is [the content of] his duty [as expressed] by commands (<s>praiṣa</s>)? — It is <s>bhāvanā</s> consisting of three aspects. // 31 //

children.text:
na hi puruṣaḥ svavyāpāraṃ muktvānyad anuṣṭhātuṃ śaktaḥ |
praiṣāś cainam anuṣṭhāpayanti |
te yadi tadvyāpāraṃ kathaṃcin nopādadyuḥ, na niyokutṃ śaknuyur ity evam api bhāvanākṣepasiddhiḥ |
yāvāṃś ca brāhmaṇagataḥ praiṣaḥ sa sarvaḥ prāptyabhāvād vidhir eva bhavatīti vināpi smaraṇena
% p. 84
kṛtyānāṃ vidhāyaktvam |
ayam eva ca vidhipraiṣayor viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a person is not capable of performing anything other than his own activity. And commands (<s>praiṣa</s>) impel him to perform. If they were not to take up his activity in some way, they would not be able to enjoin [him] — thus, even in this way, the establishment of <s>bhāvanā</s> through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>) is [demonstrated]. And whatever command occurs in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts], all of it, due to the absence of [the person's] prior entitlement, is indeed an injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) — thus, even without recourse to [the argument from] memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>), [p. 84] the <s>kṛtya</s> forms have the character of enjoining. And this very [distinction] is the difference between injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) and command (<s>praiṣa</s>):

children.text: pravartanasmṛtiḥ prāpte praiṣa ity abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: A reminder of [a duty for which there is already] impulsion, where [the person] is [already] entitled, is called a command (<s>praiṣa</s>);

children.text: aprāptapraiṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ vidhitvaṃ pratipadyate // 32 //
children.translated_text: all [impulsion] that enjoins where [the person] is not [yet] entitled assumes the character of injunction (<s>vidhi</s>). // 32 //

children.text: tasmāt pratyayārtho bhāvanety upapannam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that <s>bhāvanā</s> is the meaning of the verbal suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>).

children.text:
%p. 85
nanu ca yadi prayojakavyāpāro bhāvaneṣyate, tataḥ pacāv adhiśrayaṇādīni, yajau ca mānasaḥ saṃkalpa ityādīnāṃ bhāvanātvam, ta eva ca dhātvarthā iti dhātuvācyaiva bhāvanā syāt |
naiṣa doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: [p. 85] Objection: If <s>bhāvanā</s> is held to be the activity of the instigator (<s>prayojaka</s>), then in the case of [the root] <s>pac</s> ('to cook'), [actions like] placing on the fire (<s>adhiśrayaṇa</s>) and the like, and in the case of [the root] <s>yaj</s> ('to sacrifice'), the mental resolution (<s>mānasa saṃkalpa</s>) and the like — these would be <s>bhāvanā</s>; and these are the meanings of the verbal root — hence <s>bhāvanā</s> would be expressed by the verbal root [itself]. This is not a fault:

children.text: dhātvarthavyatirekeṇa yady apy eṣā na lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Although this [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is not observed as distinct from the meaning of the verbal root,

children.text: tathāpi sarvasāmānyarūpeṇānyāvagamyate // 33 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, it is apprehended as something different, in its universal generic form. // 33 //

children.text:
sarvatra hy adhiśrayaṇādau karotīty api sāmānyavyāpārāṃśaḥ pratīyate |
pacatyādivācyā viklittyadhiśrayaṇādayaḥ karmasthāḥ kartṛsthāś ca |
tatra yadaudāsīnyapracyutimātreṇa parispandarūpaṃ nirūpyate sā bhāvanā |
ye tu tadanurañjanasamarthāḥ kartṛkarmagatā viśeṣās te tasyā eva karaṇetikartavyatāṃśayor niviśante |
evaṃ tarhi dhātvarthasāmānyaṃ bhāvanety etad āpannam |
satyaṃ sādhyatayā sāmānyam, na tu gotvādirūpeṇa |
katham |
children.translated_text: For everywhere — in [acts like] placing on the fire and the like — the generic aspect of activity as 'doing' (<s>karoti</s>) is also apprehended. The specific actions [such as] softening (<s>viklitti</s>), placing on the fire (<s>adhiśrayaṇa</s>), and the like — as expressed by [the roots] <s>pac</s> ('cook') and the like — pertain [some] to the object and [some] to the agent. Therein, what is ascertained as mere movement (<s>parispanda</s>) through the mere cessation of indifference — that is <s>bhāvanā</s>. But those specific features pertaining to the agent and the object which are capable of coloring it — they enter into [<s>bhāvanā</s>'s] own aspects of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) and procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). If so, then it follows that <s>bhāvanā</s> is the generic [meaning] of verbal roots. True, it is generic in the sense of being what is to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), but not in the sense of being a universal like cowness (<s>gotva</s>) and the like. How so?

children.text: anyad eva hi yāgādau sāmānyaṃ karaṇātmakam /
children.translated_text: For one thing is the generic element in sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like, which has the nature of an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>);

children.text: anyac ca bhāvanā nāma sādhyatvena vyavasthitam // 34 //
children.translated_text: and another thing is what is called <s>bhāvanā</s>, which is established as what is to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>). // 34 //

children.text:
bhāvanāyāṃ hi svayam eva pratipuruṣaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣau bhavataḥ |
tathā tatkaraṇabhūte yāgādau samavetaṃ bhāvanākaraṇāṃśāpekṣitaṃ dhātvarthasāmānyaṃ nāma yat karmaśabdenābhi-
%p. 86
dhīyate |
viśeṣaṇabhāvāc ca yāgādayo bhāvanāviśeṣā ity ucyante, na tadvyaktitvena |
śāstrapradeśe tu kriyākarmaśabdau kadācid dhātvarthe prayjyete, kadācid bhāvanāyām, kadācit tu pratyāsattyobhayatrāpi prayogaḥ, na svarūpābhidhānena |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: For in <s>bhāvanā</s> itself, generic and specific [features] exist for each individual person. Likewise, in sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) and the like — which serve as instruments thereof — the generic meaning of the verbal root that is inherent [in them] and that is required by the instrumental aspect of <s>bhāvanā</s> is what is denoted by the word <s>karman</s> ('action'). [p. 86] And due to their being qualifiers, sacrifice and the like are called 'specific forms of <s>bhāvanā</s>' — not as instances of it [as a universal]. In [various] passages of the <s>śāstra</s>, the words <s>kriyā</s> ('action') and <s>karman</s> ('action/ritual') are sometimes used for the meaning of the verbal root, sometimes for <s>bhāvanā</s>, and sometimes, due to proximity, for both — not as denoting their own [essential] form. Why?

children.text: yādṛśī bhāvanākhyāte dhātvarthaś cāpi yādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>bhāvanā</s> is [as expressed] in the finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>), and whatever the meaning of the verbal root is —

children.text: nāsau tenaiva rūpeṇa kathyate 'nyaiḥ padaiḥ kvacit // 35 //
children.translated_text: that [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is never spoken of in that very form by other words anywhere. // 35 //

children.text:
bhāvanāśabdo hi niṣpannātmikāṃ sattvarūpāpannāṃ liṅgasaṃkhyāyoginīm abhidhatte |
na cāsāv ākhyāte tādṛśy abhidhīyate |
liṅgasaṃkhyārahitarūpeṇa gamyamānatvāt |
evaṃ dhātvartho 'pi veditavyaḥ |
tathā karoti bhāvayati ity etābhyām api śrutyā tāvad anyādṛg evārthaḥ pratīyate kṛñbhāvayatyarthakaraṇikā bhāvanā |
na caivaṃrūpāsau yajeta ityādiṣv astīty aparyāyatvam |
tatrānantarapratyayotthāpitabhāvanāntarabuddhim avivakṣitvārthasaṃvādaḥ kartavyaḥ |
tenādūraviprakaraṣamātreṇaiṣa prayogaḥ, nārthasāmyena---ity avasthitam ananyaśabdavācyatvaṃ bhāvanāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: For the word <s>bhāvanā</s> denotes [an entity] that has the nature of something already accomplished (<s>niṣpanna</s>), that has assumed the form of an existent entity (<s>sattva-rūpa</s>), that possesses gender and number. But [<s>bhāvanā</s>] as expressed in the finite verb is not of such a nature, because it is apprehended in a form devoid of gender and number. The same should be understood of the meaning of the verbal root. Likewise, even by the [verbs] <s>karoti</s> ('does') and <s>bhāvayati</s> ('brings about'), through the [actual] audible [form], a quite different meaning is apprehended — namely, a <s>bhāvanā</s> having the instrumentality of the meaning of [the roots] <s>kṛ</s> and <s>bhāvayati</s>. And [<s>bhāvanā</s>] of such a form does not exist in [injunctions like] <s>yajeta</s> ('he should sacrifice') and the like — hence there is no synonymy. In establishing the agreement of meaning there, one should set aside the cognition of a different <s>bhāvanā</s> aroused by the immediately adjacent suffix. Therefore, this usage [of <s>karoti</s> etc.] is only by way of approximate proximity, not by way of identity of meaning — thus it is established that <s>bhāvanā</s> cannot be expressed by any other word.

children.text:
%p. 87
sā tu pratītamātraiva prādhānyād apekṣāntarānadhīnatvāc ca prathamaṃ tāvat sādhyāṃśam apekṣate bhāvayet kim? iti |
tatra yāvatī vidhyupetā bhāvanā tasyāṃ pūrvapratītam api vidhitvaṃ tāvan nāśrīyate, yāvad aṃśatrayapūrṇā bhāvanānuṣṭhānayogyā na bhavati |
vidhitvaprakramāc ca prathamam evaitaj jñāyate---yādṛśair aṃśaiḥ pūrṇeyaṃ vidhānam arhati tādṛśaiḥ pūrayitavyā---iti |
na ca buddhipūrvakārī puruṣaḥ puruṣārtharahitaṃ vyāpāraṃ vacanaśatenāpy ukto 'nutiṣṭhati |
na ca puruṣārthaḥ sādhyavyatiriktāṃśapātitvena kaiścit prārthyate |
tato 'bhyarhitatarasyānyasya sādhyasyāvidhyamānatvāt |
tatra yady asyāṃ bhāvanāyām apuruṣārthaḥ sādhyaḥ syāt, tataḥ puruṣeṣv apravartamāneṣu pratyayasya prayojakaśaktir bādhyeta |
tena yady api samānapadopādānapratyāsatter dhātvarthaḥ sādhyāṃśapūraṇāyopaplavate, tathāpy ayogyatvān nirākriyate |
na hi pratyāsattir evaikā saṃbandhakāraṇam, yogyatvādy api. tathā ca vakṣyati yasya yenārthasambandhaḥ iti |
kiñ ca---
children.translated_text: [p. 87] But that [<s>bhāvanā</s>], being merely apprehended [through the suffix], first of all — due to its predominance and its not being dependent on any other expectancy — requires the aspect of what is to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), [i.e., the question:] 'What should one bring about?' Therein, in the case of <s>bhāvanā</s> that is accompanied by injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), even the injunctive character that was earlier apprehended is not relied upon until the <s>bhāvanā</s>, complete with its three aspects, becomes fit for performance. And from the very procedure of injunction, this is known first: 'It [<s>bhāvanā</s>] is to be filled with such aspects as make it worthy of enjoining — it should be completed with those.' And a person who acts deliberately does not carry out a purposeless activity even if told by a hundred words. Nor is the purpose of the person (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) sought by anyone as belonging to an aspect other than the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be accomplished) — because there is no other <s>sādhya</s> that is more worthy. Therein, if the <s>sādhya</s> in this <s>bhāvanā</s> were devoid of purpose for the person, then, since persons would not be impelled [to act], the motivating power of the [verbal] suffix would be contradicted. Therefore, even though the meaning of the verbal root, due to the proximity of being taken up by the same word, presents itself for filling the <s>sādhya</s> aspect, nevertheless, being unfit, it is rejected. For proximity alone is not the sole cause of connection — fitness and the like also [play a role]. And thus it will be stated: 'That with which there is a meaningful connection' (<s>yasya yenārthasambandhaḥ</s>). Moreover:

children.text: saṃbandhamātram uktaṃ ca śrutyā dhātvarthabhāvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Scripture (<s>śruti</s>) has stated only the connection between the meaning of the verbal root and <s>bhāvanā</s>;

children.text: tad ekāṃśaniveśe tu vyāpāro 'syā na vidyate // 36 //
children.translated_text: but in placing [the verbal root meaning] in one [particular] aspect [of <s>bhāvanā</s>], scripture (<s>śruti</s>) has no operation. // 36 //

children.text:
saṃbandhamātraṃ kṛtvā nivṛttavyāpārāyāṃ śrutāv anyatarāṃśaniveśo yogyatvād āśrayitavyaḥ |
tad yadi sādhyāṃśād ekapratyayopāttena pratyāsannatareṇa vidhitvena pracyāvyate,
%p. 88
tato 'ṃśāntareṇa nūnaṃ saṃbhaṃtsyata ity evaṃ patīkṣyate |
kiñ ca
children.translated_text: Since scripture, having merely established the connection, has ceased its operation, the placement in one or another aspect is to be relied upon based on fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). If, then, [the meaning of the verbal root] is displaced from the <s>sādhya</s> aspect by the injunctive character — which is closer due to being taken up in the same cognition — [p. 88] then it is expected that it will be connected with another aspect. Moreover:

children.text: sādhyāṃśe purrṣāṇāṃ ca pratyayo na niyojakaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the [verbal] suffix is not an enjoiner of persons with respect to the <s>sādhya</s> aspect;

children.text: svayam eva hi jānanti kartavyaṃ puruṣāḥ sadā // 37 //
children.translated_text: for persons themselves always know what is to be accomplished. // 37 //

children.text:
yatra hi śāstrādhīnā puruṣapravṛttiḥ, tatra tatsannikarṣaviprakarṣāv apekṣyete |
sādhyaṃ punaḥ svargapaśuputragrāmādi prāg eva śāstrāt sarve puruṣāḥ pratipadyante |
tataś ca bhāvayet kim? ity apekṣitamātre vinaiva tāvac chāstreṇaitāvad avagatam puruṣārthaḥ kaścit iti |
tatra viśeṣamātream anavagatatvād apekṣyate |
tad api ca na sādhyātmanā, kiṃ tarhi, etadbhāvanāviṣayatvena |
tataś ca dūrasthasyāpi svargāder eva kṛtāspadasya saṃgatiḥ |
dhātvarthasambandhas tv anapekṣitaḥ kriyeta |
vidhyānarthakyāc ca bādhyetatarāṃ śrutiḥ |
kiñ ca
children.translated_text: For wherever human activity depends on scripture (<s>śāstra</s>), there the proximity and remoteness [of scriptural connection] are taken into account. But the goal to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>) — heaven, cattle, sons, a village, etc. — is understood by all persons even prior to scripture. And therefore, when the mere expectation arises — 'what should one bring about (<s>bhāvayet kim</s>)?' — even without scripture, this much is already understood: 'there is some human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>).' In that regard, only the specific [identity of the goal] is expected [from scripture], since [only] that is not yet known. And even that [is expected] not in its capacity as the goal to be accomplished, but rather in its capacity as the object of the productive operation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). And therefore, even heaven etc., though remote, has its place secured [as the sādhya]. But the connection with the verbal root's meaning (<s>dhātvārtha</s>) would be unsought. And since injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) would become purposeless, the scriptural text would be overridden all the more. Moreover —

children.text: bhavane yasya kartṛtvaṃ kathaṃcid avadhāritam /
children.translated_text: That entity whose agency in becoming (<s>bhavana</s>) has been somehow determined,

children.text: svavākye vānyavākye vā sa sādhyatvaṃ prapadyate // 38 //
children.translated_text: whether in its own sentence or in another sentence — that attains the status of goal to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>). || 38 ||

children.text:
na cātra dhātvarthāder bhavanakriyāsaṃbandho 'vagataḥ |
svargādīnāṃ tu kāmaśabdopabandhād bhavanasaṃbandho vijñāyate. kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: And here, no connection of the verbal root's meaning etc. with the action of becoming is understood. But for heaven etc., the connection with becoming is known because of the association with the word <s>kāma</s> (desire). Why?

children.text: svargo me syād itītthaṃ hi svargādiḥ prārthyate bhavan /
children.translated_text: 'May heaven be mine' — thus heaven etc. is desired as [something that is to] come into being;

children.text: tenāsau bhāvanāpekṣaḥ prayojyatvena gamyate // 39 //
children.translated_text: therefore, it is understood as dependent on <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation), in the capacity of the instigated (<s>prayojya</s>). || 39 ||

children.text:
tato 'vadhṛtasvargādisādhyāṃśā bhāvanā kena bhāvayet? ity evaṃ karaṇam apekṣa-
%p. 89
te |
tatra śāstrādhīnarpavṛttitvāt tatsannikarṣādāv āśrīyamāṇe (1) pramāṇāntarāc ca yogyāyogyatvayor ajñānāt, (2) vidhyavirodhāc cātyantapratyāsattyupasthitadhātvarthātikramakāraṇābhāvāt, (3) sarvaphalabhāvanānāṃ ca kenacid dhātvarthaviśeṣeṇa vinānupapatteḥ yāgena ity evaṃ vijñāyate |
yady api ca yāgaḥ svayam eva tāvad aniṣpannaḥ, tathāpi svasādhananiṣpāditaḥ san sādhayiṣyati |
sarvam eva ca kadācin niṣpannaṃ kadācid aniṣpannam |
na ca prāk śāstrapravṛtter niṣpattiḥ kvacid upayujyate |
phalasiddhikālamātropayogitvāt karaṇaniṣpatteḥ |
pramāṇavaśāc ca trikālavartinām api sādhanatvāvirodhaḥ |
tasmād yāgādīnāṃ karaṇatvam |
tac cāpūrvadvāreṇeti tacchabdebhyo 'pūrvapratītiḥ |
tataś caivam api sūtrārthaḥ saṃbhavati---ye bhāvārthā bhāvanāprayojanāḥ karmaśabdā yajyādayaḥ, tebhyaḥ kriyā pratīyeta---iti |
nanu coktena karmakaraṇasambandhanyāyena sakarmakadhātuyuktād evākhyātād bhāvanāvagatiḥ prāpnoti |
tathā hi
children.translated_text: Then, the <s>bhāvanā</s>, whose goal-component (<s>sādhya-aṃśa</s>) consisting of heaven etc. is determined, expects its instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) [in the form of the question]: 'by what means should one bring it about (<s>kena bhāvayet</s>)?' In that regard, since activity depends on scripture, when proximity [to the scriptural statement] is considered: (1) because of ignorance of fitness and unfitness from any other means of knowledge; (2) because, due to non-opposition to the injunction, there is no reason to pass over the verbal root's meaning which is presented in closest proximity; and (3) because without some particular verbal root's meaning, the <s>bhāvanā</s> directed at any result would be impossible — therefore 'by sacrifice (<s>yāgena</s>)' is understood. And even though the sacrifice itself is as yet unaccomplished, still, being accomplished through its own means, it will accomplish [the goal]. For everything is sometimes accomplished and sometimes unaccomplished. And prior to the operation of scripture, the accomplishment [of the sacrifice] is nowhere required — since the accomplishment of the instrument is needed only at the time of the fruition of the result. And by the force of the means of knowledge, there is no contradiction in something existing across all three times serving as an instrument. Therefore the sacrifice etc. has the status of instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). And that [instrumentality operates] through the medium of <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented transcendent potency) — thus from those [scriptural] words arises the cognition of <s>apūrva</s>. And therefore the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is possible even in this way: 'From those <s>karma</s>-words (action-words) like <s>yaj</s> (to sacrifice) etc. which have the meaning of becoming (<s>bhāvārtha</s>) and serve as the purpose of <s>bhāvanā</s>, action is cognized.' But [the objector says:] by the principle of the object-instrument relation already stated, the cognition of <s>bhāvanā</s> should arise only from a verbal form containing a transitive root. And thus —

children.text: yenepsitatamair bhāvaiḥ kim ity aṃśo 'varudhyate /
children.translated_text: The 'what' (<s>kim</s>) component is secured by the most desired goals;

children.text: tadyogī tena dhātvartho na kaścit syād akarmakaḥ // 40 //
children.translated_text: and [since] the verbal root's meaning is connected with that, no [root] would be intransitive. || 40 ||

children.text:
yadi vā sarvadhātūnāṃ sakarmakatvāpattiḥ, atha vākarmakebhyo bhāvanayā na bhavitavyam |
naiṣa doṣaḥ |
kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Either all verbal roots would turn out to be transitive, or else intransitive [roots] should not have <s>bhāvanā</s>. This is not a fault. Why?

children.text: anyad eva hi dhātvarthprāpyaṃ karma sakarmake /
children.translated_text: The object (<s>karma</s>) that is to be attained by the verbal root's meaning in a transitive [root] is one thing;

children.text: anyad eva ca sarvatra pratyayārthanibandhanam // 41 //
children.translated_text: and the [object] that is the basis of the suffix's meaning (<s>pratyayārtha</s>) is quite another thing, applicable everywhere. || 41 ||

children.text:
odanaṃ pacati, grāmaṃ gacchati iti dhātvarthāpavargalabhyam ekaṃ karma, aparaṃ punar bhāvanākarma |
(1) tatra kadācid dhātvarthakarmaiva bhāvanākarmatvam api pratipadyate pākenaudanaṃ bhāvayati iti |
(2) kadācit punaḥ svakarmaviśiṣṭadhātvarthayuktā bhāvanā karmāntareṇa yujyate grāmagamanena svārthaṃ bhāvayati, odanapākena ceti |
tac caitad dhātvarthāt paratas tadavāpyamātratvena gamyamānaṃ dhātvarthāntatirohitam api bhāvanākarmatayā sarvatrāvadhāryate |
tac ca prāyeṇaivaṃkāmaśabdenaiva saṃbandham āpadyate sukhakāma āsīta, svāsthyakāmaḥ śayīta iti |
saty api āsiśetyor akarmakatve yaḥ pratyayena karotyartho 'bhihitaḥ, tatkarmatvena svādīny avadhāryante |
tena (1) karoteḥ sarvadā sakarmakatvāt,
(2) akarmakākhyātānām api ca tatsāmānādhikaraṇyadarśanāt kiṃ karoti āste, kiṃ karoti śete iti---siddhaivamādiṣv api sakarmikā bhāvanā |
children.translated_text: <s>Odanaṃ pacati</s> ('he cooks rice'), <s>grāmaṃ gacchati</s> ('he goes to the village') — one object is obtained as the completion of the verbal root's meaning; but the other is the object of <s>bhāvanā</s>. (1) In that regard, sometimes the very object of the verbal root's meaning also takes on the role of the <s>bhāvanā</s>-object — as in <s>pākenaudanaṃ bhāvayati</s> ('through cooking he brings about rice'). (2) But sometimes the <s>bhāvanā</s>, combined with the verbal root's meaning qualified by its own object, is connected with a different object — as in <s>grāmagamanena svārthaṃ bhāvayati</s> ('through going to the village he brings about his own purpose'), or <s>odanapākena ca</s> ('and through cooking rice'). And this [bhāvanā-object], understood as merely what is to be attained beyond the verbal root's meaning — though hidden beyond the verbal root's meaning — is determined everywhere as the object of <s>bhāvanā</s>. And it most often enters into a relationship with the word <s>kāma</s> (desire) in this way: <s>sukhakāma āsīta</s> ('one desiring happiness should sit'), <s>svāsthyakāmaḥ śayīta</s> ('one desiring health should recline'). Even though <s>ās</s> (to sit) and <s>śī</s> (to recline) are intransitive, the <s>karoti</s>-meaning expressed by the suffix determines happiness etc. as its object. Therefore: (1) because <s>karoti</s> is always transitive; and (2) because even intransitive verbal forms show co-reference with it — <s>kiṃ karoti? āste</s> ('What does he do? He sits'), <s>kiṃ karoti? śete</s> ('What does he do? He reclines') — the <s>bhāvanā</s> with an object is established even in these [intransitive] cases.

children.text: yajer api tu yat karma pūjyatvād devateṣyate /
children.translated_text: But as for the object of <s>yaj</s> (to sacrifice) — the deity, which is said [to be the object] because of being the one to be honored —

children.text: tadujjhitvaiva putrādeḥ karmatvaṃ bhāvanāśritam // 42 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned that, the object-status pertaining to [goals like] sons etc. depends on <s>bhāvanā</s>. || 42 ||

children.text:
tasmāt sakarmakākarmakayor aviśeṣāt āsanena bhāvayet ity api prayogasiddhiḥ |
kas tarhi sakarmakākarmakayor bhedaḥ |
ucyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since there is no distinction between transitive and intransitive [in this respect], the usage <s>āsanena bhāvayet</s> ('one should bring about [the goal] through sitting') is also established. What then is the difference between transitive and intransitive? We say —

children.text: sākṣād avyabhicāreṇa dhātvartho yatra karmabhāk /
children.translated_text: The root whose meaning directly and invariably has an object

children.text: sakarmakaḥ sa dhātuḥ syāt pāraṃparye tv akarmakaḥ // 43 //
children.translated_text: is a transitive root; [one that has an object only] indirectly is intransitive. || 43 ||

children.text:
%p. 91
āsanaśayanādīnāṃ hi na niyamenānantaryeṇa vā idam tat iti vā karma nirūpyate, tenākarmakā abhidhīyante |
pacigamyādīnāṃ tu viklidyattatsaṃyujyamānasākṣātsaṃbandhikarmāvyabhicārāt sakarmakatvam |
na tu bhāvanāviśeṣaṇatve kaścid viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: For sitting, reclining, and the like have no object that is determined invariably, or immediately, or as 'this specific thing' — therefore they are called intransitive. But <s>pac</s> (to cook), <s>gam</s> (to go), and the like, because of the invariable [presence of a] directly related object — that which softens, that with which [one] is connected — are transitive. But there is no difference with respect to their being qualifiers of <s>bhāvanā</s>.

children.text:
seyaṃ bhāvanāṃśadvayaparipūrṇā satī sarvakaraṇānām upāyānanugṛhītānāṃ karaṇatvānupapatteḥ kathaṃ bhāvayet itītikartavyatām apekṣate |
sā ca pratyakṣādīnām anugrāhakadarśanaśaktyabhāvād atyantaśāstragamyeti yathāsannikarṣaṃ tadasaṃbhavāc ca yathā kathaṃcid upasthāpyamānā śāstrānusāreṇa śrutyādyupadeśena codanāsāmānyādyatideśena vātyantādṛṣṭopakāradvāreṇānyathānupapattyā kalpyate |
tataḥ paripūrṇatvād anuṣṭhātuṃ yogyeti vidhīyate |
tadvidhānāc cārthāpattyā yāgādividhānam---ity upapannaṃ bhāvārthasūtram |
children.translated_text: This <s>bhāvanā</s>, when complete with its two components [sādhya and karaṇa], since instruments that are not supported by a method cannot have the status of instruments, expects the procedural details (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) [in the form of the question]: 'how should one bring it about (<s>kathaṃ bhāvayet</s>)?' And since perception and the other [means of knowledge] lack the capacity to reveal what supports [the ritual procedure], it is entirely knowable only from scripture. And since [scripture] is to be applied according to proximity, and where that is not possible, then in whatever way it is presented — following scriptural guidance, through the teaching of <s>śruti</s> (revelation) etc., or through extension (<s>atideśa</s>) from the general nature of injunction — it is construed by the force of otherwise inexplicable means, through a completely unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) benefit. Then, being complete, it becomes fit for performance, and is thus enjoined. And from the injunction of that [bhāvanā], the injunction of sacrifice etc. follows by implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — thus the <s>sūtra</s> on bhāvārtha is established.

children.text:
%p. 92
bhavanti kecit karmaśabdāḥ---yāgaḥ yajanam ijyā ity udāhartavye tatsāmānādhikaraṇyasiddhaśyenaikatrikādyudāharaṇaṃ yāgādikaraṇatvacodanottarakālabhāvikarmaśabdatvena pāratantryāt sujñānam |
svatantrāṇāṃ kathaṃcid api bhāvārthatvāśaṅkāsaṃbhavāt |
yāgādayo hi svātantryeṇāpi kadācid anumānād bhāvārthāśaṅkāviṣayāḥ syur iti |
children.translated_text: There are certain <s>karma</s>-words (action-words): when one should give examples like <s>yāga</s> (sacrifice), <s>yajana</s> (sacrificing), <s>ijyā</s> (offering), the citing of examples like <s>Śyena</s>, <s>Ekatrika</s>, etc. — which are established through co-reference with those — is easily understood, because they are action-words that come into being after the injunction that posits the sacrifice etc. as instrument, and hence are dependent. Because for independent [action-words], there could not even be the suspicion of having bhāvārtha in any way. For sacrifice etc. might independently, through inference, come within the scope of suspicion of having bhāvārtha.

children.text:
kecid bhāvārthā na karmaśabdāḥ---yathā bhāvayet kuryāt iti codāharaṇam |
bhūtyādayas tu prayojyavyāpāravacanatvān naiva yathāvarṇitabhāvārthā ity anudāharaṇam |
tatra yathā kathaṃciṇ ṇijantavyutpattyā bhāvaśabda eko nīyeta, netarau |
tāv api tu prayojyavyāpārāṃśena kathaṃcid bhāvārthāv ity udāhṛtau |
atha vā dvitīyasūtrārthavyākhyānena bhāvanāprayojanatvam aṃśavācitvenāstīti vināpi sakalārthābhidhānād bhavanti bhāvārthāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some [words] have bhāvārtha but are not <s>karma</s>-words — as exemplified by <s>bhāvayet</s> ('one should bring about') and <s>kuryāt</s> ('one should do'). But <s>bhūti</s> etc., because they denote the instigated activity (<s>prayojya-vyāpāra</s>), do not have bhāvārtha as described above — hence they are not cited [as examples]. There, the word <s>bhāva</s> alone could be somehow led [to this meaning] through the derivation of the <s>ṇijanta</s> (causative), but not the other two. However, those two also, through the component of instigated activity, are in some way of bhāvārtha — hence they are cited. Alternatively, by the explanation of the meaning of the second <s>sūtra</s>, since having bhāvanā as purpose exists [even] through partial denotation — even without denoting the complete meaning — [words] are of bhāvārtha.

children.text:
kathaṃ punar amī na karmaśabdāḥ, yadā dhātumātraṃ karmaśabdatvenoktam |
nirviśeṣasya sāmānyasyānuṣṭhātum aśakyatvād akarmaśabdatvam |
ato viśeṣavācinām eva dhātūnāṃ karmaśabdatvāśrayaṇād acodyam etat |
children.translated_text: But how are these not <s>karma</s>-words, when it has been stated that the verbal root alone is a <s>karma</s>-word? [Answer:] Because the general, undifferentiated [root] cannot be performed, it is not a <s>karma</s>-word. Therefore, since only roots that express specific [actions] are taken as <s>karma</s>-words, this objection carries no weight.

children.text:
%p. 93
yadi hi śyenacitrādarśapaurṇamāsaśabdāḥ phalaiḥ saṃbadhyeran, tato yāgasya karaṇatvābhāvāt tatsāmānādhikaraṇyanimittanāmadheyatvānupapatteḥ prasiddhyādibhir guṇavidhitvam eva syāt |
ataḥ sthita etasminn adhikaraṇe ity āha |
kasmāt punar idaṃ tatraiva na nītam |
pramāṇalakṣaṇenāsaṃbandhāt |
atha nāmadheyatvaṃ kasmād atra nānīyate |
bhedalakṣaṇenāsaṃbandhāt |
tasmād yathānyāsam eva sthitayor arthāt paurvāparyasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: For if words like <s>Śyena</s> (Hawk[-sacrifice]), <s>Citradarśa</s>, and <s>Paurṇamāsa</s> (Full-moon [sacrifice]) were to be connected with the result (<s>phala</s>), then — since sacrifice would lack instrumentality, and since the name based on co-reference with that [sacrifice] could not be established — they would be merely subsidiary injunctions (<s>guṇavidhi</s>) by virtue of [general] knowledge etc. Therefore, this section (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) stands as established, he says. But why was this [topic] not taken up in that very [section]? Because it has no connection with the criterion of means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇalakṣaṇa</s>). And why is the topic of name-designation (<s>nāmadheyatva</s>) not brought here? Because it has no connection with the criterion of differentiation (<s>bhedalakṣaṇa</s>). Therefore, with both [sections] standing as arranged, the sequential order is established by implication.

children.text:
na caiṣām arthinā iti phalapadābhiprāyam |
vivibhaktitvāt iti saṃbandhanimittākhyātavibhaktivigamāt |
atha vā niṣpannārthābhidhāyisubvibhaktiviśeṣayogo vivibhaktitvam |
tasmān na dravyādiśabdānāṃ phalasaṃbandha iti |
āha ca
children.translated_text: And [the phrase] 'not of these by the desirer' (<s>na caiṣām arthinā</s>) has the sense of the word 'result' (<s>phala</s>). 'Because of being separated from inflection' (<s>vivibhaktitvāt</s>) means: because of the absence of the verbal inflection that is the cause of the [syntactic] connection. Alternatively, <s>vivibhaktitva</s> means: the conjunction with a particular <s>sub</s>-inflection (noun-suffix) that denotes an accomplished meaning. Therefore, substance-words and the like have no connection with the result. And he says —

children.text: sādhyasādhanasaṃbandhaḥ sarvadā bhāvanāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The relation of goal to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>) and means (<s>sādhana</s>) always rests upon <s>bhāvanā</s>;

children.text: tena tasya na siddhiḥ syād bhāvanāpratyayād ṛte // 44 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the establishment of that [relation] cannot occur without the verbal suffix conveying <s>bhāvanā</s>. || 44 ||

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bhāvo 'rtha iti cet || Jaim_2,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of all, <s>bhāva</s> (becoming) is the meaning' — if [one argues] so — || <s>Jaimini</s> 2.1.2 ||

children.text: na tāvat pratyayasyeṣṭam apūrvapratipādanam /
children.translated_text: It is not accepted that the suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>) conveys <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented);

children.text: na ca dhātoḥ svatas tat syān nāmno vā parataḥ samam // 45 //
children.translated_text: nor can the root (<s>dhātu</s>) convey that by itself, nor equally can the noun. || 45 ||

children.text:
yadi bhāvanāvacanasyaivāpūrvapratipādakatvam iṣyate dhātor vā pratyayanirapekṣasya, tato nāmapakṣo durbalaḥ syāt, iha tu yathaiva dhātoḥ pratyayasaṃbandhānugṛhītasya bhāvanā-
%p. 94
nurañjananimittaṃ karaṇavācitvaṃ bhavati, evaṃ nāmapadasyāpīty aviśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: If it is held that the <s>bhāvanā</s>-expression (productive operation) itself is the conveyor of <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen transcendent result), or that the verbal root alone, independent of the suffix, [conveys it], then the noun-view (<s>nāmapakṣa</s>) would be weak. But here, just as the verbal root, supported by its connection with the suffix, has the quality of denoting instrumental means (<s>karaṇa</s>) through the coloring (<s>anurañjana</s>) of <s>bhāvanā</s>, similarly the noun-word too [has this quality] — hence there is no difference.

children.text: yeṣām utpattau sve prayoge rūpopalabdhis tāni nāmāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ parākāṃkṣā bhūtatvāt sve prayoge || Jaim_2,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Those [words] at whose origination [i.e., when used] the perception of the [referent's] form [occurs] in their own usage — those are nouns (<s>nāma</s>). Therefore, from them there is no expectation [of further meaning], because [their referent] is already existent (<s>bhūta</s>) in their own usage. || <s>Jaimini</s> 2.1.3 ||

children.text:
yad uktam yadaikasmād apūrvaṃ tadetarat tadarthaṃ bhaviṣyati iti tadgataṃ tāvad vastudharmeṇa viśeṣaṃ darśayati |
katham |
children.translated_text: What was stated — 'when from a single [word] <s>apūrva</s> is established, the other, being subordinate thereto, will serve its purpose' — regarding that, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] shows the distinction by way of the nature of the thing (<s>vastudharma</s>). How?

children.text: bahvadṛṣṭaprasaṅgād dhi dharmo neṣṭaḥ pade pade /
children.translated_text: Because of the unwanted consequence of many unseen entities (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) [being required], <s>dharma</s> [derived] from word to word is not desired;

children.text: nāmnaḥ phalena saṃbandhe parihāro na tasya ca // 46 //
children.translated_text: and when the noun has a connection with the result (<s>phala</s>), there is no remedy for that [problem either]. // 46 //

children.text:
ekasmād adṛṣṭe kalpite yadītarad dṛṣṭārthatvena tādarthyaṃ bhajate tato lāghavaṃ labhyate |
atha tu tādarthyasiddhaye tato 'pi punar adṛṣṭaṃ kalpyata eva tato varaṃ phalenaiva sarvāṇi saṃbaddhāni |
na ca saṃbandhavairūpyakleśāśrayaṇam |
nāmnaś ca phalasaṃbandhe 'vaśyaṃ dhātvarthas tadanugrahārtho 'bhyupagantavyaḥ |
sa ca svayaṃ niṣpādyaḥ siddharūpasya nāmārthasya na śaknoti dṛṣṭenopakartum |
na hi nāmārthas tam apekṣate |
śabdaprayogavelāyām eva niṣpannatayā gamyamānatvāt, apekṣaṇīyasya vā siddhatvenāyogyatvāt |
children.translated_text: If, when <s>apūrva</s> is postulated from a single [word], the other, by having a seen purpose (<s>dṛṣṭārtha</s>), partakes of subordination [to the first], then parsimony (<s>lāghava</s>) is obtained. But if, for the establishment of that subordination, yet another unseen [element] must be postulated from that too, then it is better that all [words] are connected with the result directly. And there is no resort to the difficulty of dissimilarity of connection. And when the noun has a connection with the result, the meaning of the verbal root (<s>dhātvārtha</s>) must necessarily be accepted as serving to support it. But that [verbal root meaning], being itself something-to-be-accomplished (<s>niṣpādya</s>), cannot assist the already-accomplished (<s>siddharūpa</s>) noun-meaning through a seen [connection]. For the noun-meaning does not depend on it — because at the very time of word-usage it is understood as already accomplished; or because that which would be depended upon is itself already accomplished, hence unsuitable [as a means].

children.text:
prayujyate 'smin iti cābhidheya eva prayogaḥ |
tadādhāraiva hi niṣpannarūpopalabdhiḥ |
anutpannatve kriyārūpasya vaktavye vināśitvapradarśanaṃ niṣpannasyāpi
%p. 95
kṣaṇikatvena punaḥ punar niṣpattyapekṣopapatteḥ |
tebhyaḥ parākāṅkṣā anyākāṅkṣā niṣpādyatvena vā pradhānākāṅkṣā na vidyata ity adhyāhāraḥ |
atha vā tebhyaḥ parā dūre ākāṅkṣety arthaḥ |
kutaḥ |
bhūtatvāt iti svarūpakathanārtham upanyastaṃ niṣpannatvād eveti punar ante tad eva hetutvenopadiṣṭaṃ sūtrakāreṇa |
children.translated_text: And 'usage' (<s>prayoga</s>) is precisely in the referent (<s>abhidheya</s>) [itself] — for the perception of an accomplished form has its basis precisely in that [referent]. The [opponent's] demonstration of destructibility when the form of action is said to be non-arisen — [does not succeed, because] even of what is accomplished, due to momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), there is justification for depending on arising again and again. 'From them there is no expectation (<s>parākāṅkṣā</s>)' — [means] there is no other expectation, or no primary expectation in the sense of [their meaning] being something-to-be-accomplished; this should be supplied. Alternatively, 'from them the expectation is far (<s>parā dūre</s>)' — this is the meaning. Why? 'Because of being already existent (<s>bhūtatvāt</s>)' — this is cited for the purpose of stating the nature [of noun-meaning]; 'because of being already accomplished' — this very same [reason] is again taught at the end as the cause by the <s>sūtrakāra</s>.

children.text: yeṣāṃ tūtpattāv arthe sve prayogo na vidyate tāny ākhyātāni tasmāt tebhyaḥ pratīyetāśritatvāt prayogasya || Jaim_2,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: But those [words] at whose origination there is no usage in the referent — those are finite verbs (<s>ākhyāta</s>). Therefore, from them [the meaning] is understood, because the usage depends upon [them, i.e., their meaning is not yet accomplished]. || <s>Jaimini</s> 2.1.4 ||

children.text: ākhyātavartī dhātvarthaḥ sādhyarūpaḥ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: The meaning of the verbal root (<s>dhātvārtha</s>), being of the nature of something-to-be-accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), is understood

children.text: tasmin phalavatīṣṭe tu nāmno dṛṣṭārthateṣyate // 47 //
children.translated_text: as occurring in the finite verb (<s>ākhyāta</s>). When that [verb-meaning] is desired as having a result, the noun is held to have a seen purpose (<s>dṛṣṭārtha</s>). // 47 //

children.text:
dhātvarthas tāvat prakṛtyaiva sādhyātmakaḥ |
viśeṣatas tv ākhyātagatena dhātunocyamānaḥ sa yadi phalasādhanatvena codyate tato 'siddharūpatvāt tasya sādhanākāṅkṣāyāṃ satyāṃ nāmapadaṃ guṇavidhitvena nāmadheyatvena vobhayathāpi dṛṣṭenaiva tādarthyaṃ labhate |
nanu nāmadheyapakṣe nāmapadam api sādhyārthaṃ bhaviṣyatīti dhātutulyaṃ syāt |
na |
tasya phalasaṃbandhe guṇavidhitvena siddhārthatvāt |
api ca
children.translated_text: The meaning of the verbal root, by its very nature (<s>prakṛtyā</s>), is of the nature of something-to-be-accomplished (<s>sādhyātmaka</s>). Specifically, when that [meaning], expressed by the root occurring in the finite verb, is impelled as the means of accomplishing the result (<s>phalasādhana</s>), then — because of its unaccomplished nature (<s>asiddharūpatva</s>), when there is an expectation of means (<s>sādhanākāṅkṣā</s>) — the noun-word, whether as a qualifying injunction (<s>guṇavidhi</s>) or as a name (<s>nāmadheya</s>), in both ways obtains subordination through a seen [connection] alone. [Objection:] But on the <s>nāmadheya</s> view, the noun-word too would have an unaccomplished meaning, and thus be like the verbal root. [Reply:] No — because when connected with the result, it has an accomplished meaning by virtue of being a qualifying injunction. Moreover —

children.text: sādhyātmako 'pi dhātvartho yadā nāmnābhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: Even though the meaning of the verbal root is of the nature of something-to-be-accomplished, when it is denoted by a noun-word,

children.text: tadā dravyavad evāsau niṣpannātmā pratīyate // 48 //
children.translated_text: then, just like a substance (<s>dravya</s>), it is understood as having an accomplished nature (<s>niṣpannātman</s>). // 48 //

children.text:
yady api vastusvarūpeṇa dhātvarthaḥ sādhyaḥ, tathāpi nāmapadenocyamāno liṅgasaṃkhyāyogitvāt siddharūpo 'bhidhīyate |
abhidhānakṛtā cākāṅkṣotpattir na vastukṛtā |
tasmād yuktā dhātor evākāṅkṣā na nāmna iti |
children.translated_text: Even though by the nature of the thing (<s>vastusvarūpa</s>) the verbal root-meaning is to-be-accomplished, nevertheless, when expressed by a noun-word, because of its connection with gender (<s>liṅga</s>) and number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), it is denoted as having an accomplished form. And the expectation (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>) arises from the mode of expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>), not from the nature of the thing. Therefore, the expectation is rightly from the verbal root (<s>dhātu</s>) alone, not from the noun.

children.text:
kiñ cāśritatvāt prayogasya iti |
adhunā śabdapratyāsattikṛto viśeṣo 'bhidhīyate |
puruṣavyāpārātmikāyāṃ hi bhāvanāyāṃ dhātvarthopaśleṣo 'pi puruṣeṇāśritas tadatikramahetvabhāvāc ca na nāmapadagrahaṇam |
tasmād asti viśeṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'because the usage depends upon [the verb] (<s>āśritatvāt prayogasya</s>).' Now the distinction caused by verbal proximity (<s>śabdapratyāsatti</s>) is stated. For in <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive operation) whose nature is human activity (<s>puruṣavyāpāra</s>), the connection with the verbal root-meaning (<s>dhātvarthopśleṣa</s>) too depends upon the person [as agent]; and because there is no cause for transgressing that [connection], there is no apprehension of the noun-word [as primary]. Therefore, there is a distinction.
